We introduce SHARPnP, an interpretable, flexible framework coupling registration and reconstruction for RGB-guided hyperspectral super-resolution from noisy, unaligned measurements without clean references. We adapt a pretrained registration model via a cross-view loss backpropagated through a fixed plug-and-play fusion module. Temporal and recorrupted pairs enable reference-free self-supervision on noisy inputs. At test time, we calibrate cross-camera radiometry and refine alignment. Plug-and-play fusion employs sequential three-band denoising. On the REAL benchmark, SHARPnP outperforms supervised fusion baselines at $4\times$, $8\times$, and $16\times$ on clean inputs and at $4\times$ under Gaussian noise ($σ=5/255, 10/255$). On native RGB-HSI snapshot measurements, it reconstructs all 51 VIS-NIR bands, beyond the conventional 31-band VIS setting, without high-resolution references.

title: Can a Frontier LLM Repair a Quantized Network by Tool-Free Weight-Space Programming?
text: Can a Frontier LLM Repair a Quantized Network by Tool-Free Weight-Space Programming?. We give four large language models (LLMs) of the Claude family the complete weights of a 20k-parameter CIFAR-10 CNN as text and ask them to produce a 4-bit network without tools, data or the ability to run inference. Standard round-to-nearest (RTN) quantization to 4 bit lowers the test accuracy from 81.4% to 60.4%. We design four evaluation protocols that differ in the input and task description given to the LLMs and analyze their responses. In the first two protocols the LLMs are given the float and the 4-bit RTN network and are told that the accuracy has dropped significantly. In the last two they receive only the float network and the task to quantize it, which tests whether they apply an optimization on their own or fall back to plain RTN. Our analysis shows that a frontier LLM can recover most of the lost accuracy. Given one answer per layer, Opus 5.5 raises the accuracy of the 4-bit network to 77.95% by balancing the rounding errors within each 3x3 kernel, reasoning over the integer weights without tools. This is 3.5 pp below the float network and 2.8 pp below AdaRound, which learns the rounding from calibration data. Given only the float network, the LLMs name error-cancelling corrections but do not apply them and fall back to plain RTN, at most with mildly clipped scales, which still lifts Fable 5.2's quantized network to 70.0%. We analyze in detail what the LLMs did and why it works. Code and prompts can be found at https://github.com/urbste/weight-space-programming-ptq

title: SALSA: Sampling Adversarial Suffixes from Learned Distributions for LLM Safety Assessment
text: SALSA: Sampling Adversarial Suffixes from Learned Distributions for LLM Safety Assessment. Large language models (LLMs) remain vulnerable to jailbreak attacks, where adversaries append optimized suffixes to otherwise benign looking prompts to bypass safety alignment. Existing optimization-based GCG-style attacks can be effective, but they are expensive at inference time, and suffer from poor transfer. We present, SALSA, a generative framework that learns a distribution over jailbreak suffixes from optimization-derived attack corpora. Once trained, the model supports efficient sampling-based attacks. On open-source targets, it achieves attack success rates comparable to state-of-the-art optimization baselines, while reducing generation time from 3.46s to 0.04s per prompt. In black-box transfer, it remains highly effective against proprietary systems, including 99% ASR on GPT-3.5-Turbo, and reaches 45% ASR on the substantially harder GPT-4o, more than doubling the strongest baseline at an equal sampling budget. We further offer an intuition for why generative sampling can preserve high attack success, when the learned suffix distribution is close to the distribution of optimization outputs. Overall, our results show that learning adversarial suffix distributions yields a scalable, and practically efficient foundation for continuous LLM vulnerability discovery.

title: Score-Based Diffusion for Hypergraph Signals in the t-Spectral Domain
text: Score-Based Diffusion for Hypergraph Signals in the t-Spectral Domain. We introduce the first score-based generative model for signals on a fixed hypergraph, formulated in the spectral domain of t-product hypergraph signal processing (t-HGSP). The naive tensor heat semigroup is ill-posed, since after palindromic symmetrization the spectral slices of the Laplacian tensor are no longer positive semidefinite. A per-mode frequency shift repairs it, yielding a forward Ornstein-Uhlenbeck diffusion that decouples per (eigenmode, slice) pair with closed-form marginals, exact score targets, and an exactly isotropic stationary law. A lightweight slice-conditioned denoiser is trained on the resulting real spectral grid. Sampling combines its score on data-active modes with the closed-form score elsewhere, which proves essential for stability at scale. A closed cosine-form observation operator turns missing-node recovery into linear-Gaussian guidance with stabilized posterior sampling. On hypergraphs of up to 500 nodes, our model beats a clique-expansion baseline by margins growing from $2\times$ to $27\times$ in covariance error, matches the graph-spectral statistics of the data better than the graph-basis model itself, and reaches the finite-sample estimation floor on data rotated off the t-spectral axes. Posterior sampling reduces missing-node NMSE to 0.28-0.64 (classical baselines 0.87-1.1) at conservative coverage, and cuts the framework's own denoising baseline by up to $3.6\times$.

title: Low-regularity evolution and control for the nonlinear Schrödinger equation with singular bilinear interactions
text: Low-regularity evolution and control for the nonlinear Schrödinger equation with singular bilinear interactions. We consider the one-dimensional nonlinear Schrödinger equation (NLS) $i\dt ψ-\dx^2 ψ= (u(t)\cdot μ) ψ+κ|ψ|^{2m}ψ,$ on the torus under the presence of singular, time-dependent bilinear external fields $(u(t)\cdot μ)$. We prove well-posedness in $H^s(\T)$ for low regularity indices $s>\max\big\{\tfrac12-\tfrac1m,0\big\}$ ($s>0$ when $κ=0$), under sharp assumptions on the singular potentials, covering both the linear and nonlinear cases. We establish small-time exact controllability in $H^{\frac12+}(\T)$ for a large class of states, by combining saturation techniques with the moment method. The result extends previous bilinear exact controllability results for linear Schrödinger equations, which are typically obtained in large time and under high regularity assumptions. Crucial to our approach is the role of the singular time-dependent potentials, which enable the recovery of controllability properties in small time and at low regularity, overcoming obstructions present in the smooth setting.

title: Efficient reconfiguration, polynomial decompositions and approximate counting
text: Efficient reconfiguration, polynomial decompositions and approximate counting. We consider reconfigurations of integer assignments to planar lattice regions that preserve specified line totals, which are motivated by questions of combinatorial construction, algorithmic sampling and approximate counting. An elementary prototype is provided by contingency tables, i.e. two-dimensional grids of non-negative integers with prescribed row and column sums, which can be reconfigured by basic switches of the form $\left(\begin{smallmatrix}1&-1\\-1&1\end{smallmatrix}\right)$. More difficult combinatorial instances include reconfiguration of Latin squares or queens configurations. Our main technical ingredient is the following polynomial decomposition lemma. Fix a positive integer $k$. Let $F(x)\in \mathbb{Z}[x]$ be a polynomial of degree at most $n$ such that $(1-x)^k\mid F(x)$ and the sum of the absolute values of the coefficients of $F$ is $m$. We prove that $F$ can be written as a sum of $O(m+n)$ basic polynomials of degree at most $n$ of the form $\pm x^a(1-x^{a_1})\cdots (1-x^{a_k})$ where $a,a_1,\ldots,a_k$ are non-negative integers. The proof uses the existence of a miraculous high-dimensional coupling of signed distributions on cross polytopes that has independent interest. We will apply this lemma to questions of combinatorial construction in other papers; in this paper we illustrate its application to approximate counting.

title: Brauer classes of representations of division algebras and their Langlands parameters
text: Brauer classes of representations of division algebras and their Langlands parameters. For every depth-zero supercuspidal representation $π$ of $\mathrm{GL}_n(K)$ with algebraic-valued central character, we prove that the Brauer obstructions to realizing its Jacquet-Langlands transfer and its normalized Langlands parameter $\varphi_π\otimes|\cdot|^{-(n-1)/2}$ over their common field of rationality $E=\mathbb{Q}(π)$ sum to $(n-1)[B_{p,\infty}\otimes_{\mathbb{Q}} E]$. Here $K/\mathbb{Q}_p$ is finite, the transfer is to the units of the central division algebra over $K$ of invariant $1/n$, and $B_{p,\infty}$ is the quaternion algebra over $\mathbb{Q}$ ramified exactly at $p$ and $\infty$. We conjecture this identity without the depth restriction. For arbitrarily large $n=p-1$, we construct simple supercuspidal representations satisfying the same sum formula. Their transfers have finite-order central character and Schur index $n$, whereas their normalized parameters have index $n/2$. Since these transfers are not self-dual, the unequal indices contradict the isomorphism of Schur algebras conjectured by Prasad and Ramakrishnan.

title: Max-degree filtration, Koszul complexes, and Multicolor Permutation Wordle
text: Max-degree filtration, Koszul complexes, and Multicolor Permutation Wordle. We explore the Koszul resolutions of a family of ideals, each generated by multivariate polynomials that split completely into linear factors. The motivating examples come from the game Permutation Wordle of Kutin and Smithline, as analyzed by Kutin, Smithline, and Vatter, and an open question, Conjecture 4.5 in Kutin and Smithline's work on Multicolor Permutation Wordle. For each ideal in this family, with our chosen generators, the Koszul differentials are strict for the max-degree filtration and, more generally, at every multidegree whose coordinates form a set of consecutive integers. The resulting dimension count resolves Kutin and Smithline's conjecture. The proof is an induction in which each inductive step is an iteration. The core argument is human generated. The present proof, developed with AI assistance, separates the iteration of multidegree reductions from the mapping cone induction. This method avoids the need to chase compatibility of lifts up to the top grade of the complex.

title: Global Existence and Large-Time Behavior of Strong Solutions to the Two-Dimensional Full Compressible Navier-Stokes Equations with Degenerate Heat Conductivity
text: Global Existence and Large-Time Behavior of Strong Solutions to the Two-Dimensional Full Compressible Navier-Stokes Equations with Degenerate Heat Conductivity and Large Initial Data. In this paper, we investigate the two-dimensional full compressible Navier--Stokes system with degenerate heat conductivity in three settings: the periodic domain, a general bounded simply connected domain subject to Navier-slip boundary conditions, and the whole space with non-vacuum far-field density. We assume that the shear viscosity $μ$ is a positive constant, the bulk viscosity $λ(ρ)\ge0$ depends on the density, and the heat conductivity takes the form $κ(θ)=κ_0 θ^α$ with $κ_0>0$. For a broad class of density-dependent bulk viscosities, we establish the global existence and large-time behavior of strong solutions for arbitrarily large initial data allowing vacuum. In particular, our results include the sublinear growth law $$ λ(ρ)=\fracρ{(1+ρ)^\varepsilon \log\log(e^e+ρ)}, $$ where $\varepsilon>0$ is a sufficiently small constant depending only on the domain, the initial data, and the physical parameters.

title: Large blow-ups of uniform hypergraphs
text: Large blow-ups of uniform hypergraphs. Let \(k\ge2\), let \(H\) be a fixed \(k\)-uniform hypergraph on \(h\) vertices with at least one edge, and let \(a>0\). We prove that every sufficiently large \(n\)-vertex \(k\)-uniform hypergraph with at least \(a n^h\) copies of \(H\) contains a blow-up of \(H\) with at least \(b(\log n)^{1/(k-1)}\) vertices in each part, where \(b=b(H,a)>0\). The exponent of $\log n$ is best possible. This answers a question of Rödl and Schacht and proves a conjecture of Bollobás, Erdős and Simonovits from 1976. For fixed \(q\ge2\) and \(0<α<1/2\), it follows that every \(q\)-coloring of the \(k\)-subsets of \([n]\) contains a set of order \((\log n)^{1/(k-1)}\) on which one color has density at least \(1-α\). For triples this recovers the sharp bound of Conlon, Fox and Sudakov. For \(k\ge4\), this improves their general exponent to the optimal value \(1/(k-1)\) and answers a 1990 question of Erdős for which he offered a \$500 prize.

title: Properties of the Sawin--Wood Model for Unramified Galois Groups of Global Fields
text: Properties of the Sawin--Wood Model for Unramified Galois Groups of Global Fields. We prove almost-sure finite generation and finite presentation in the pro-$|Γ|'$ $Γ$-category for the Sawin--Wood measure $ν_{Γ,n,U}$, where $Γ$ is a non-trivial finite group, $n$ is coprime to $|Γ|$, and $U$ is a nonempty multiset of conjugacy classes of $Γ$. The $Γ$-generator rank of the random group $X$ has the sharp tail $\mathbf{P}(d_Γ(X) \geq r) = Ce^{-κr^2-ζr}(1+O(e^{-\varepsilon r}))$, where $C>0$, $κ>0$, and $ζ\in\mathbb{R}$ are explicit constants depending on $n$, $Γ$ and $U$, and $\varepsilon>0$. Almost surely, $X$ admits a presentation with the minimum number of $Γ$-generators, using at most $|U|$ more defining $Γ$-relations than generators. We also prove that every open subgroup of $X$ has finite abelianization almost surely under the assumption that for every complex representation of $Γ$ there is an element in $U$ that fixes a nonzero vector. Finally, we prove that $H_2(X,\widehat{\mathbb{Z}})=0$ almost surely when $n=1$, $Γ$ is cyclic, and $U$ contains only the conjugacy class of a generator of $Γ$ (with multiplicity one).

title: $S$-preclones and the Galois connection ${}^S\mathrm{Pol}$-${}^S\mathrm{Inv}$, Part II: Boolean $\pm$-preclones
text: $S$-preclones and the Galois connection ${}^S\mathrm{Pol}$-${}^S\mathrm{Inv}$, Part II: Boolean $\pm$-preclones. We continue the investigation of $S$-preclones initiated in Part I, specializing to the case of Boolean $\pm$-preclones where $S = \{+,-\}$ is the two-element group and the base set is $A = \{0,1\}$. The main results include the complete classification of maximal and minimal Boolean $\pm$-preclones in the lattice ${}^{\pm}\mathcal{L}_2$ of all Boolean $\pm$-preclones. We prove that there are exactly nine maximal Boolean $\pm$-preclones. Hence we obtain a completeness theorem for $\pm$-preclones: a set of $\pm$-operations generates all $\pm$-operations if and only if it contains an operation that fails to preserve each of the nine defining $\pm$-relations of the maximal $\pm$-preclones. Next we classify the twenty minimal Boolean $\pm$-preclones (atoms of the lattice), each described via a generating $\pm$-operation. We also investigate self-dual $\pm$-preclones, characterizing the eight maximal and nine minimal self-dual $\pm$-preclones and proving a corresponding completeness theorem. Additionally, we include the result, due to Vojtěch David, that the lattice ${}^{\pm}\mathcal{L}_2$ is uncountable, in contrast with the countability of the classical Post lattice of Boolean clones. This is established by embedding an uncountable poset of clonoids into ${}^{\pm}\mathcal{L}_2$. Finally, we study preimage classes of classical Boolean clones within ${}^{\pm}\mathcal{L}_2$, providing complete descriptions for the unary case and for several non-unary minimal clones. We also prove a Baker--Pixley type theorem for $\pm$-preclones containing the majority operation, showing that such $\pm$-preclones are determined by their binary $\pm$-relations.

title: Stochastic Taylor expansions for Volterra equations and their geometry
text: Stochastic Taylor expansions for Volterra equations and their geometry. We develop series representations for solutions to general nonlinear controlled and stochastic Volterra equations in terms of two new types of signature, called geometric and Itô Volterra signature. These signatures collect the necessary iterated kernel integrals and satisfy (quasi) shuffle identities, which allow us to prove universal approximation results for Volterra path functionals. We then derive finite order expansions with precise remainder terms for both controlled and stochastic Volterra equations with possibly singular kernels, as well as expansions of their expectations. For the latter, we provide sufficient conditions for absolute convergence of the resulting series representation and verify them for polynomial Volterra processes. As an application, we propose a weak approximation principle for stochastic Volterra equations based on matching low-order expected signature coordinates of the kernel. Numerical experiments for Volterra-Jacobi processes demonstrate promising performance.

title: Undershoot of h-fold sumsets: Apéry spectra, similar ordering and the three-distance theorem
text: Undershoot of h-fold sumsets: Apéry spectra, similar ordering and the three-distance theorem. For a finite set $A_0\subset\mathbb{N}$ with $0\in A_0$, $\max A_0=d$ and $\gcd(A_0)=1$, and a target $T$, the undershoot at level $h$ is the distance from $T$ down to the largest element of the $h$-fold sumset $hA_0$ not above $T$. Its total over $T\in[0,hd]$ is bounded in $h$: for large $h$ it equals the sum of the masses of two numerical semigroups attached to $A_0$, where the mass adds $L(L+1)/2$ over the maximal runs of $L$ gaps. We describe how the total reaches this limit: it can rise to it, fall to it, or climb past it and return. When the monomial curve of $A_0$ is arithmetically Cohen-Macaulay, two Apéry sets give every undershoot exactly, and partial sums of a fixed spectrum bound the total from below, with equality at every level exactly when two threshold sequences are similarly ordered; the total then rises concavely to its limit, reached exactly at the sumsets regularity. We characterize the similarly ordered four-element sets. For $\{0,a,b,2b\}$ with $0<a<b$ coprime, the three-distance theorem gives the total in explicit quadratic pieces. A non-Cohen-Macaulay set exceeds its limit at every failing level $h$ with $hd$ at least the sum of the two conductors; every such four-element set does so, and a five-element example never does. For arbitrary sets, finite corner data give the exact undershoot over any window.

title: Quantitative $p$-Wasserstein bounds for empirical measures on manifolds: Expectation and concentration
text: Quantitative $p$-Wasserstein bounds for empirical measures on manifolds: Expectation and concentration. We derive quantitative bounds in expectation and concentration for the $p$-Wasserstein distance between the empirical measure of independent samples and their common law on metric measure spaces satisfying the measure contraction property $\MCP(K,n)$, with $K\le0$. Our results extend the expectation estimates of Boissard--Le Gouic (Theorem 1.1 in Ann. Inst. Henri Poincaré Probab. Stat. 50 (2014), no. 2, 539--563) and the concentration estimates of Bolley--Guillin--Villani (Theorem 2.1 in Probab. Theory Relat. Fields 137 (2007), 541--593). In spaces with exponential volume growth, suitable exponential moment assumptions allow us to recover the Euclidean rate $N^{-1/n}$ in expectation when $n>2p$. As an application, we obtain uniform-in-time concentration estimates for the empirical measure of McKean--Vlasov interacting particle systems on complete Riemannian manifolds with Ricci curvature bounded below by combining comparison theory and parallel coupling to a noninteracting proxy system.

title: A lower bound on the Nusselt number in stochastically forced Rayleigh--Bénard convection
text: A lower bound on the Nusselt number in stochastically forced Rayleigh--Bénard convection. We establish a lower bound on the expected long-time averaged Nusselt number for two-dimensional Rayleigh--Bénard convection at infinite Prandtl number, with free-slip boundaries and a suitable additive noise of amplitude $0 0$ depend only on the domain parameter $L$. Without noise, no such bound can hold, since the conductive state is a solution with $Nu=1$ for every Rayleigh number. The proof uses the auxiliary functional method. For general Markov processes, we show that the defining inequality of an auxiliary functional need only hold after a short time average. This reduces the problem to showing that, with uniformly positive probability, the solution quickly leaves the set of states with low heat flux and low thermal dissipation. We establish this by projecting onto an unstable eigenvector of the linearization around the initial mean temperature profile, yielding a one-dimensional Itô process with linear growth, additive noise, and nonlinear error terms.

title: On Presburger Arithmetic Expanded with Prime Numbers
text: On Presburger Arithmetic Expanded with Prime Numbers. We prove unconditionally that the first-order theory of Presburger arithmetic expanded by a predicate for the primes is undecidable. Bateman, Jockusch and Woods proved this in 1993 assuming Dickson's conjecture. We use the counter-machine framework of Karimov, Nieuwveld and Ouaknine and their idea of using `arbitrary permutations', and the number-theoretic input comes from Hildebrand and Maier's 1988 proof that the limit points of $k$ consecutive normalised prime gaps have positive measure. We use a discrete version, which they obtain before limits are taken. The key lemma is that although Hildebrand and Maier's result does not seem to give arbitrary permutations of consecutive prime gaps, it gives arbitrary permutations for the differences $p_i - q_i$ for two finite blocks of consecutive primes $p_0 < \cdots < p_k$ and $q_0 < \cdots < q_k$. Moreover, with the same key lemma, we show that Presburger arithmetic expanded with the function that maps $n$ to the $n$th prime defines multiplication.

title: Positive Geometry of Oriented Matroid Strata
text: Positive Geometry of Oriented Matroid Strata. We study the positive geometry of Grassmannians whose boundary is a union of Plücker divisors. For the full Plücker boundary the regions are closures of realization spaces of uniform oriented matroids. In rank three we show that the pair $(\mathrm{Gr}_{3,n},Z_{3,n})$ is a positive arrangement in the sense of Sturmfels and Telen for $n\le 9$ points and compute its combinatorial rank from point counts of the configuration space $\mathcal{X}_{3,n}$ over finite fields. For seven points the canonical forms of the regions span all logarithmic forms. For eight points they do not, because the Möbius-Kantor configuration is not realizable over the reals. This determines for seven and eight points whether the integrands of Cachazo, Early and Zhang for the generalized biadjoint amplitudes of Cachazo, Early, Guevara and Mizera span the space of logarithmic forms. From ten points on, the genus is positive because a K3 surface appears in the boundary. For smaller boundaries and arbitrary rank we give a recursion that adds one point at a time and preserves the genus and the combinatorial rank. It recovers the positive Grassmannian and shows that realization spaces of stacked polytopes are regions of positive arrangements of combinatorial rank one.

title: On the phase-space geometry for Riemann solutions: rank-one structure, implicit solutions and elusive transitional shocks
text: On the phase-space geometry for Riemann solutions: rank-one structure, implicit solutions and elusive transitional shocks. The effective flux function reduces a Riemann problem for a $2\times 2$ system of conservation laws to a scalar one, by lifting the wave curve. We show that the reduction rests on a rank-one property, namely that the Jacobian $\partial(u,\,v)/\partial(x,\,t)$ equals the product of the two wave strengths, up to nonzero factors, and vanishes identically for every self-similar solution. Hence the lifting needs no hypothesis for Riemann data, and for Cauchy data it survives exactly on an integral curve of an eigenvector field, where we give an implicit solution; off that curve the state path leaves it at a rate we compute. We then ask when an implicit closed-form solution exists for arbitrary data. For homogeneous quadratic fluxes these are precisely the systems linearly equivalent to two decoupled Burgers equations (the curve $a=1+b^2$ of the Schaeffer--Shearer normal form). Every such system loses strict hyperbolicity along a full line, so no model with an isolated umbilic point qualifies, among them the quadratic Corey model of three-phase flow. We close with a quadratic model in which a datum on a straight integral curve gives an exact solution with a stationary transitional shock, having one family nearly linearly degenerate at each end.

title: The Kelvin--Hicks Formula from the Energy--Casimir Principle
text: The Kelvin--Hicks Formula from the Energy--Casimir Principle. The classical Kelvin--Hicks formula expresses the propagation speed of a thin vortex ring in an incompressible ideal fluid in terms of its circulation, distance from the symmetry axis, and core radius. In this paper, we rigorously derive this formula from a variational principle based on Arnold's energy--Casimir method, without prescribing any of these geometric or physical quantities a priori. We introduce a scale-invariant variational principle involving the energy, impulse, and $L^p$ Casimir invariants. For $1 < p < \infty$, we construct orbitally stable energy-maximizing vortex rings and investigate how their geometry depends on the Casimir exponent $p$. For sufficiently large $p$, the vortex rings have cores homeomorphic to a ball and converge to Hill's spherical vortex as $p \to \infty$. In contrast, as $p\to1^+$, the energy-maximizing vortex rings concentrate onto a circular filament of radius $e^{1/3}$, uniquely selected by the variational principle. After suitable translations and rescalings, their vortex-core profiles converge to an optimizer of the logarithmic Hardy--Littlewood--Sobolev inequality. Introducing an effective core radius $ε_p$ determined by the entropy of the vorticity distribution, we establish the Kelvin--Hicks formula \begin{align*} W_p = \frac{Γ_p}{4πR_p} \left(\log\frac{8R_p}{ε_p}-1+o(1)\right) \quad \textrm{as}\ p\to1^+, \end{align*} where $W_p$, $Γ_p$, and $R_p$ denote the propagation speed, circulation, and effective ring radius, respectively. In particular, the constant correction $-1$ is obtained for nonuniform vortex-core profiles without imposing any prescribed core structure.

title: Convexification effects of $L_p$-sums
text: Convexification effects of $L_p$-sums. It is a classical result, quantified by Shapley, Folkman, and Starr, that the Minkowski averages of any compact set asymptotically approach its convex hull in the Hausdorff metric. In this paper, we investigate the analogous convexification phenomenon for the Firey $L_p$-sums of compact sets. First, we establish new structural properties of the $L_p$-sum. Notably, we show that the iterated $L_p$-sum of compact sets whose convex hull contains the origin is eventually starlike. We then study $L_p$-convexification for three classical measures of nonconvexity: Hausdorff metric, volume deficit, and effective standard deviation. For each of these measures, we prove that the $k$-fold $L_p$-sum averages of a compact set $A$ converge to $\text{conv}(0,A)$ when $1<p<\infty$, and to $\text{conv}(A)$ when $p=\infty$. In each case, we show that the convergence to the convex hull is eventually monotone. For the Hausdorff metric and effective standard deviation, we prove sharp upper bounds for the $L_p$-sum of two compact sets.

title: Finite-time blowup in the inviscid GOY and Sabra models
text: Finite-time blowup in the inviscid GOY and Sabra models. For the inviscid GOY and Sabra shell models with zero boundary conditions at the lowest shells, we construct strong solutions with finitely supported initial data whose vorticity amplitudes blow up in the supremum norm in finite time, at the self-similar rate $(T-t)^{-1}$. The blowup is stable under small perturbations of the initial data in the same norm, including complex-valued ones. Guided by the work of Mailybaev, we use a travelling wave of the renormalized equations to obtain blowup in the original variables. We construct such a wave for the equations extended to all integer shells, decaying in both directions. We then show that the dynamics near this wave contract once the directions generated by time-translation and phase symmetries are removed by adjusting the symmetry parameters at each step (a modulation argument). This yields blowup solutions on the positive shells satisfying the original boundary conditions. Computer-assisted interval arithmetic is used to establish the existence of the travelling wave and the contraction estimate needed for the modulation argument.

title: Even Quartets and the Maximum Density of a Simplical 3-Cocycle
text: Even Quartets and the Maximum Density of a Simplical 3-Cocycle. Colour the triples of an $n$-element set red or blue, and call a four-set even if it contains an even number of red triples. We prove that the minimum number of even four-sets is $\frac5{16}\binom n4-Θ(n^3)$. In particular, the maximum asymptotic density of a simplicial $3$-cocycle over the field of two elements is $11/16$. The classical two-part matrix construction attains the limiting bound. We prove that it also determines the unique limiting distribution of quartet parities on every fixed number of vertices. Writing $m_n$ for the minimum density, we bound the limit inferior and limit superior of $n(5/16-m_n)$ between $0.75$ and $0.752427$. The lower bound on even quartets follows from an exact rational inequality on eight vertices. A perturbation of the construction explains all $72$ cases of equality in this finite inequality, of which only $22$ survive in an extremal limit.

title: Positive recurrence of weakly reversible stochastic reaction networks with mass-action kinetics
text: Positive recurrence of weakly reversible stochastic reaction networks with mass-action kinetics. We study finite stochastic reaction networks with mass-action kinetics. A network is weakly reversible if every reaction lies on a directed cycle of complexes. We prove that, for arbitrary positive rate constants, the Markov chain of every such network is non-explosive and positive recurrent on each communicating class. This settles the long-standing chemical recurrence conjecture. The proof is by construction of a Lyapunov function. For a fixed choice of weights on the species, the function is the exponential of a weighted count of the molecules, adjusted by a bounded quantity which is defined through the paths of reactions leading back to a reference population, and which accounts for the species that are absent or scarce. Before the adjusted count can decrease, several preparatory steps may be needed. We count faster and slower steps separately, giving priority to paths that require fewer slow steps. Weak reversibility controls how competing reactions can change these counts. Finitely many choices of weights are then combined, and a minimization over a scale parameter gives a single function on each communicating class.

title: Spanning cyclability of split graphs
text: Spanning cyclability of split graphs. For a positive integer $k$, a graph $G$ is called $k$-spanning cyclable (resp. $k$-edge spanning cyclable) if, given any $k$ distinct vertices $v_1, v_2, \ldots, v_k$ (resp. $k$ independent edges $e_1, e_2, \ldots, e_k$) of $G$, there exist $k$ vertex-disjoint cycles $C_1, C_2, \ldots, C_k$ in $G$ such that $v_i \in V(C_i)$ (resp. $e_i \in E(C_i)$) for each $i$ and $V(C_1) \cup \cdots \cup V(C_k) = V(G)$. In particular, the notion of 1-spanning cyclable coincides with the existence of a Hamiltonian cycle, and a Hamilton-connected graph is necessarily 1-edge spanning cyclable. For a positive integer $r \ge 3$, a graph $G$ is $K_{1,r}$-free if $G$ does not have an induced subgraph isomorphic to $K_{1,r}$, and $K_{1,4} + e$ denotes the graph obtained by adding an edge $e$ between two nonadjacent vertices of $K_{1,4}$. There are several interesting conjectures and sparse results relative to these conjectures on Hamiltonian properties of $K_{1,r}$-free split graphs, whose vertex set can be partitioned into a maximum clique $W$ and an independent set $J$. In this paper, we extend some of these results by proving the following: (1) every $(k+1)$-connected $K_{1,3}$-free split graph of order at least $4k-1$ is $k$-spanning cyclable for $k \ge 1$; in particular, every 2-connected $K_{1,3}$-free split graph of order at least 3 is Hamiltonian; (2) every $2k$-connected $K_{1,3}$-free split graph is $k$-edge spanning cyclable for $k \ge 2$; (3) every $(k+1)$-connected $\{K_{1,4}, K_{1,4}+e\}$-free split graph with $|W| \ge |J| \ge 3k+5$ is $k$-spanning cyclable for $k \ge 1$; in particular, every 2-connected $\{K_{1,4}, K_{1,4}+e\}$-free split graph with $|W| \ge |J| \ge 8$ is Hamiltonian; (4) every $2k$-connected $\{K_{1,4}, K_{1,4}+e\}$-free split graph with order at least $4k+9$ is $k$-edge spanning cyclable for $k \ge 2$.

title: Mirror flow for semimartingale optimal transport
text: Mirror flow for semimartingale optimal transport. Semimartingale optimal transport arises in a wide range of applications, including mathematical finance and flow-based generative models. A recurring computational challenge is that the dual energy functional is often poorly conditioned with respect to the dual potential, leading to slow convergence of gradient descent algorithms. To address this issue, we investigate a mirror flow approach that effectively preconditions the dual energy functional. We establish the geometric convergence of the mirror descent sequence. To obtain a practical numerical algorithm, we introduce a feasible discrete-time scheme based on first-order linearization. We prove that the scheme is well-defined and establish a uniform-in-time error bound for the accumulated linearization error, under a suitable smallness condition on the initial error. Finally, we apply the proposed mirror flow scheme to the specific-entropic martingale optimal transport (SEMOT) problem \cite{BuetGolfouseEtAl2026SEMOT} and observe a substantial improvement in computational efficiency.

title: Convergence of Implicit Particle Methods for Wasserstein Gradient Flows
text: Convergence of Implicit Particle Methods for Wasserstein Gradient Flows. In this paper, we establish the convergence of implicit particle methods for Wasserstein gradient flows as the number of particles tends to infinity, with the time step held fixed. The schemes combine the Jordan--Kinderlehrer--Otto (JKO) variational time discretization with particle approximations of the evolving probability measure. The main challenge lies in approximating the internal energy, which depends nonlinearly on the probability density and cannot, in general, be evaluated directly on empirical measures. We consider three approaches: a one-dimensional density reconstruction based on the spacings between ordered particles; a blob method using kernel-based density reconstruction; and a transport-map formulation in which the density is recovered from the pushforward relation through the change-of-variables formula. The latter two approaches apply in arbitrary spatial dimensions without requiring the spatial domain to be compact. For the blob method, we also establish simultaneous convergence as the particle number tends to infinity and the regularization parameter vanishes, under the scaling $N\varepsilon_N^d\to\infty$. Our analysis combines $Γ$-convergence and compactness arguments to establish convergence of the discrete variational problems and their minimizers. These results complement classical dynamical mean-field theory by providing a variational particle-to-continuum limit for implicit JKO schemes involving nonlinear internal energies.

title: Quadratic Wasserstein transport for elliptical distributions
text: Quadratic Wasserstein transport for elliptical distributions. The quadratic Wasserstein distance between Gaussian distributions is given by the classical Bures-Wasserstein formula, which depends only on the means, the covariance matrices $Σ_0$ and $Σ_1$, and their interaction $K=(Σ_0^{1/2}Σ_1Σ_0^{1/2})^{1/2}$. The same formula holds for elliptical distributions with a common radial law. In this paper, we extend this representation to general elliptical distributions by identifying an additional transport cost $Γ$ that depends on the radial laws and the spectrum of $K$. We describe $Γ$ via a weighted quadratic transport problem involving Dirichlet distributions and show that optimal couplings preserve directions within the eigenspaces of $K$. When $K$ has a single eigenvalue, we obtain an explicit cost formula and an optimal Monge map. For general spectra, we derive remarkably tight lower and upper bounds for $Γ$ using nested spectral projections and Knothe-Rosenblatt couplings. The lower bound is based on one-dimensional integrals and can be computed fast. For Gaussian, Student-$t$, uniform ball, and uniform sphere distributions, the upper bound also admits computationally efficient representations via dynamic programming. Numerical experiments demonstrate that we reduce the gap between the previously known bounds by more than 80% in many settings, and by over 99.9% in certain scenarios, even in dimension $10^6$. These improvements are particularly valuable in high-dimensional or heavy-tailed settings, where accurate numerical computation of quadratic Wasserstein distances is challenging.

title: A $2$-adic Kida-type formula for chromatic Selmer groups of elliptic curves and applications to quadratic twists
text: A $2$-adic Kida-type formula for chromatic Selmer groups of elliptic curves and applications to quadratic twists. Let $E$ be an elliptic curve over $\mathbb{Q}$ with good supersingular reduction at $2$. We study the chromatic ($\sharp/\flat$) Selmer groups of $E$ over the cyclotomic $\mathbb{Z}_2$-extension of $\mathbb{Q}$, defined using Sprung's chromatic Coleman maps. We show that at least one of these Selmer groups is $Λ$-cotorsion and, assuming the vanishing of the corresponding $μ$-invariant, establish a $2$-adic Kida-type formula describing the change in the Iwasawa $λ$-invariants under base change from $\mathbb{Q}$ to a real quadratic field $F$ in which $2$ is unramified. When $E$ has square-free conductor, applying this formula to $E$ and its quadratic twist $E^D$ yields an explicit formula describing the variation of the chromatic $λ$-invariants under twists by positive square-free integers $D\equiv1\pmod4$. As an application, under suitable hypotheses on the root number and chromatic Iwasawa invariants of $E$, we construct explicit sets of primes $\ell$ such that the $2^{\infty}$-Selmer group of $E^{\ell}$ over $\mathbb{Q}$ has $\mathbb{Z}_2$-corank one, and determine their positive natural densities.

title: Ordering Information in Multispecies Long-Range Swap Processes
text: Ordering Information in Multispecies Long-Range Swap Processes. We measure how much the left-to-right species order $W_t$ of interacting particles on the integer lattice reveals about their initial configuration. For distinct species under long-range swaps, deleting stronger particles gives coordinates with independent Poisson increments. For a finitely supported initial law, the mutual information between any function $U$ of the initial configuration and $W_t$ is $C_U/t+O(t^{-3/2})$ as $t\to\infty$, where $C_U$, which may vanish, is determined by the means of Gaussian order statistics and the conditional means of the initial compressed coordinates given $U$. On consecutive sites with a uniform initial order, we compute the coefficient of the $t\log(1/t)$ term in the short-time information loss for arbitrary species counts. For three particles in this setting, repeating the weaker rather than the stronger species triples the long-time $t^{-1}$ coefficient, although both compositions have the same composition entropy and initial-order entropy. These long-time coefficients are the same whether equal particles block or push each other, but the nonuniform limiting output law is reversed. In the ordinary multispecies totally asymmetric simple exclusion process (TASEP), two distinct particles at fixed sites with a uniform initial order instead give $t^{-1/2}$ decay.

title: Large deviation principle of error of Euler--Maruyama method for stochastic differential equations
text: Large deviation principle of error of Euler--Maruyama method for stochastic differential equations. We study large deviations for the error of the Euler--Maruyama method applied to a one-dimensional stochastic differential equation with $C_b^3$ coefficients and a uniformly elliptic diffusion coefficient. We prove that the error at the terminal time, without rescaling, satisfies a large deviation principle (LDP) at speed $n$, where $n$ is the number of steps, with a good rate function that vanishes only at the origin. In particular, the probability that the error exceeds a fixed level decays exponentially in $n$. Two effects determine the rate function. A single Brownian increment of fixed nonzero size has finite cost at speed $n$, and the cumulative effect of smaller Brownian increments depends on the states at which their squares accumulate. To capture both effects, we introduce, for a cutoff $\varepsilon\in(0,1]$, an empirical enhanced control that records the state-dependent quadratic variation of the small increments together with the time, state and size of each increment exceeding $\varepsilon$. We prove an LDP for the empirical enhanced control for every fixed $\varepsilon$, and deduce the LDP for the error by the contraction principle and an exponentially good approximation as $\varepsilon\to0$.

title: An Asymptotically Sharp Form of the Overfull Conjecture
text: An Asymptotically Sharp Form of the Overfull Conjecture. Let $G$ be a simple graph with maximum degree $Δ$. A subgraph $H$ of $G$ is \emph{$Δ$-overfull} if $|E(H)|>Δ\lfloor |V(H)|/2\rfloor$. The Overfull Conjecture, proposed by Chetwynd and Hilton in 1986, states that a graph $G$ with $Δ>|V(G)|/3$ is of class~2 if and only if it contains a $Δ$-overfull subgraph. This conjecture would give a polynomial-time algorithm for determining the chromatic index in this degree range and would imply several longstanding conjectures on critical graphs. In this paper, we prove that, for every $\varepsilon>0$, a sufficiently large graph $G$ with $Δ\ge(1/4+\varepsilon)|V(G)|$ is of class~2 if and only if it contains a $Δ$-overfull subgraph. Consequently, the chromatic index can be determined in polynomial time in this range. We also obtain the Just-overfull and Vertex-splitting Conjectures for large graphs, and Vizing's Independence Number, Average Degree, and $2$-Factor Conjectures in the same degree range. The coefficient $1/4$ is asymptotically best possible: for every odd integer $Δ\ge3$, we construct a connected class~2 graph on $4Δ+5$ vertices with maximum degree $Δ$ and no $Δ$-overfull subgraph.

title: A sufficient criterion for ballistic behavior of forced geometric motions in random environment
text: A sufficient criterion for ballistic behavior of forced geometric motions in random environment. We introduce a sufficient criterion for ballistic motion of interface evolutions in random environments. More precisely, we consider interfaces moving by forced mean curvature flow in dimension $d=2$ with a spatially fluctuating (possibly negative) driving force. Such models arise e.g. from the motions of dislocation lines or magnetic domain walls in a material with impurities. We show that the evolution admits an `effective minimum speed on large scales' if for a sample of the random environment in some long and thin box there is a sufficiently large probability that an interface initialized in the bottom of the box evolves to reach its top. The concept of an `effective minimum speed on large scales' was introduced and is required for the quantitative stochastic homogenization result in the companion paper ``Quantitative homogenization of forced geometric motions through random fields of obstacles''. We show that our criterion and hence the requirements for the homogenization result in the companion paper are satisfied for compactly supported obstacle shapes distributed according to a Poisson point process with sufficiently low intensity.

title: A Classification of Trees Without Unique Subgraphs
text: A Classification of Trees Without Unique Subgraphs. We study trees without unique subgraphs, in both the induced and non-induced settings. Graphs without unique induced subgraphs, called anchor-free graphs, form a natural candidate class for counterexamples to the Graph Reconstruction Conjecture, but their structure remains poorly understood. We develop a framework for studying anchor-free graphs based on a covering lemma that characterizes anchor-freeness via induced subgraph coverings of vertices. Using this framework, we prove that a tree is anchor-free if and only if it is a path with one less vertex than a prime. We also introduce the related notion of unique-subgraph-freeness, which acts as an edge-based analogue of anchor-freeness. We show that the line graph of every unique-subgraph-free graph is anchor-free and obtain a complete classification of unique-subgraph-free trees as either prime paths, stars, or extended stars. Together, these results provide a classification of trees without unique subgraphs and suggest a general approach for extending the theory beyond trees.

title: Two-Scale Diffusion Approximations for Many-Server Queues with Overdispersed Arrivals
text: Two-Scale Diffusion Approximations for Many-Server Queues with Overdispersed Arrivals. We study steady-state diffusion approximations for a many-server queue driven by overdispersed arrivals from a doubly stochastic Poisson process. Its arrival intensity follows a generalized Cox--Ingersoll--Ross (CIR) process, where $α\in [0, 1)$ governs how the arrival-count variance scales as $λ^{1+α}$ with the baseline arrival rate $λ$ under Taylor's law. For $α> 0$, arrival-intensity fluctuations grow faster with $λ$ than counting fluctuations from arrivals and departures, so normalizing by $λ^{(1+α)/2}$ pairs a nonvanishing intensity volatility with a vanishing queue-length volatility. This two-scale formulation differs critically from conventional diffusion approximations, which either apply a single $λ^{1/2}$ scaling with nonvanishing volatilities or drop the vanishing queue-length noise in the heavy-traffic limit. Retaining both scales, we compare two diffusions: one replaces the scaled intensity with its limiting Ornstein--Uhlenbeck (OU) process, and the other preserves the exact CIR intensity. Using Stein's method, we establish steady-state error bounds for smooth test functions of arbitrary polynomial growth that depend on $α$ in opposite directions. Both diffusions achieve the classical $O(λ^{-1/2})$ rate at $α= 0$. For $α\in (0, 1)$, however, the OU rate degrades to the sharp order $O(λ^{-(1-α)/2})$, whereas preserving the CIR intensity improves the rate to $O(λ^{-(2+α)/4})$. Our proofs establish new derivative bounds for the associated Poisson equations that remain valid when the diffusion has vanishing volatility and nonsmooth drift.

title: Unbounded GHZ dimension from fixed-order multiphoton sources
text: Unbounded GHZ dimension from fixed-order multiphoton sources. We study the local dimension of Greenberger--Horne--Zeilinger (GHZ) states obtained by selecting events with one photon per output path. Each coherent source emits photons with a fixed internal label into a distinct set of paths, and the sets for each label partition the outputs. For two-photon sources, the maximum local dimension is 2 for every even number of paths greater than 4. However, we show that three-photon sources can produce GHZ states of arbitrarily large local dimension. To prove this, we view the three paths fed by each source as an edge of a $3$-uniform hypergraph, so that accepted emission patterns correspond exactly to perfect matchings. We construct such hypergraphs with arbitrarily many edge-disjoint perfect matchings, one per label, and no others. The construction extends to $r$-uniform hypergraphs for every fixed $r\ge3$, yielding a GHZ dimension that grows at least polynomially as the number of paths ranges over the positive multiples of $r$.

title: Erdős Distance Results for $k$-Degenerate Graphs with $m$ Edges
text: Erdős Distance Results for $k$-Degenerate Graphs with $m$ Edges. The Erdős distinct distances problem asks how many distinct distances $N$ points must determine. In the plane, Guth and Katz determined the optimal power of $N$. A natural generalization fixes a finite graph $G$ with $m$ edges and records, over all injective embeddings of $G$ into a finite point set $P \subset \mathbb{R}^d$, the vectors of edge-lengths realized; we write $Δ_G^\circ(P)$ for this set of edge-distance vectors. Taking $G$ to be a single edge recovers the classical problem. In the plane, the exponent $|V(G)|-1$ is known up to an arbitrarily small loss for every connected graph. A graph is $k$-degenerate if its vertices can be ordered so that each has at most $k$ neighbors among those preceding it. We show that if $G$ is $k$-degenerate, then for every $d \ge \max(2k,3)$ and every $\varepsilon > 0$, $|Δ_G^\circ(P)| \gtrsim_{G,d,\varepsilon} N^{m/(d-1)-\varepsilon}$ for $|P|=N\ge |V(G)|$. For a connected graph with $m/(|V(G)|-1)>2(d-1)/d$, the exponent $m/(d-1)$ exceeds the spanning-tree exponent predicted by the pinned-distance conjecture. Our result is motivated by the threshold $\frac{d+k}{2}$ obtained by Borges, Foster, Ou, Palsson, and Romero Acosta for edge lengths of $k$-degenerate graphs in fractal sets. The proof combines a bisector-energy estimate for pinned $k$-stars with an entropy argument of Katz--Tardos type, applied along a construction order of $G$ and combined with an induction on the dimension.

title: The one-velocity Baer--Nunziato system as a weak limit of solutions to a compressible two-fluid system
text: The one-velocity Baer--Nunziato system as a weak limit of solutions to a compressible two-fluid system. We study how a macroscopic mixture arises from two compressible fluids that share a velocity but occupy disjoint regions. We fix the initial density profiles and the common initial velocity, and let the partition between the fluids oscillate on increasingly fine scales. The fluids remain segregated as they evolve, but in the weak limit the phase indicator becomes a volume fraction that may lie strictly between zero and one. For independent adiabatic exponents $γ^\pm\geq9/5$, we prove that the sequence of segregated solutions converges to a global weak solution of the viscous one-velocity Baer--Nunziato system in three space dimensions. The mixture pressure is the volume-weighted average of the two phase pressures, while their difference drives the evolution of the volume fraction along the flow and contributes to dissipation in the macroscopic energy inequality.

title: Uniform Algebraic Degeneracy of Entire Curves into Complex Projective Varieties
text: Uniform Algebraic Degeneracy of Entire Curves into Complex Projective Varieties. This paper is devoted to the algebraic degeneracy of entire curves intersecting a simple-normal-crossing divisor on smooth projective varieties over C, within the logarithmic Green-Griffiths-Lang program. For negativelytwisted global logarithmic jet differentials, we introduce an intrinsic weighted conormal filtration along each positive-dimensional closed boundary stratum, with weights prescribed by the contact orders along boundary components. Applying the maximal Harder-Narasimhan slopes of logarithmic cotangent bundles and the normal degrees of the strata, we define an integer vanishing threshold which can improve the pole bound obtained from the slope-based ceiling. Under the stable-base-locus hypothesis for the logarithmic Semple tower, we then establish an improved second main theorem whose counting coefficients depend on the boundary stratum, actual contact orders and the ratio of source weight to twisting exponent. These coefficients are independent of the powers used to realize the stable base locus. We further derive a uniform algebraicdegeneracy criterion allowing positive corrected pole coefficients, formulated via a finite system of stratumwise inequalities together with the ampleness of a residual divisor class. This yields conditional orbifold Green-Griffiths-Lang type statements. Refinements arising from conormalbundle decompositions and sharp local pole estimates at surface boundary crossings are established. Our examples exhibit strict improvement over naive slope-based bounds and illustrate that full-weight poles can persist at boundary crossings, and furnish concrete instances satisfying the stablebaselocus hypothesis.

title: Theta Functions and Intrinsic Mirrors of Laurent Phenomenon Algebras
text: Theta Functions and Intrinsic Mirrors of Laurent Phenomenon Algebras. We construct bases of upper Laurent phenomenon algebras over a field by minimizing Newton polytopes in a single seed. For any translation-invariant total order on the exponents, each least exponent $a$ that occurs determines a smallest Newton polytope $Q_a$. Choose one element with Newton polytope $Q_a$ and least term $x^a$ for each such $a$. These elements form a basis. In every reachable seed chart, every Gauss valuation takes a nonzero basis expansion to the minimum of its values on the nonzero summands. Suppose the algebra has Laurent coefficients and smooth spectrum over an algebraically closed field of characteristic zero. After setting the curve parameters to one, we compute theta products on the intrinsic mirror from the exchange polynomials and give a finite presentation of the mirror algebra. A seed has a polynomial corner if each exchange polynomial can be multiplied by a unit of the coefficient ring to give a polynomial with constant term one. At such a corner, order the exponents by a weight with strictly positive, rationally independent coordinates. For every lattice exponent $a$ and integral weight $p$, the theta function indexed by $p$ has least $a$-weight $\min_{b\in Q_a}\langle b,p\rangle$ in the corresponding mirror chart. This reciprocity holds for cyclic exchanges and arbitrary pole orders. For fixed exchange supports and constant terms one, we determine when the mirror is smooth and the second mirror recovers the original algebra in the chosen torus coordinates. The coefficient tuples for which both conditions hold form a computable finite set. All their entries are positive integers.

title: How to facet a gemstone: from potential modularity to modularity lifting
text: How to facet a gemstone: from potential modularity to modularity lifting. Let $F$ be a totally real field and $p\ge7$ a prime unramified in $F$. We prove that a potentially modular $p$-adic representation of $G_F$ which is potentially crystalline with distinct Hodge--Tate weights above $p$, and whose reduction is modular, non-dihedral and satisfies the usual Taylor--Wiles hypothesis, is modular. This removes the hypotheses of [MF] on the Serre weights: the multiplicity-free hypothesis, and the exclusion of Steinberg weights. The same method applies to potentially semistable representations. The proof combines the identity of cycles of [MF] with the modularity of lifts whose local components are mixed along an extension in which $p$ splits. These lifts exist by a theorem of Emerton, Gee, Pan and Zhu, they are potentially automorphic by a theorem of Calegari, Emerton and Gee, and their modularity is proved by tensoring with lifts of an auxiliary residual representation of a different weight: the tensor products lie on a common component of a local deformation ring for $\GL_4$, a lifting theorem of Thorne applies, and the factors of an automorphic tensor product are modular by [Die26].

title: Irreducibility, inertia and invertibility of the eccentricity matrices of unicyclic graphs
text: Irreducibility, inertia and invertibility of the eccentricity matrices of unicyclic graphs. The eccentricity matrix of a connected graph $G$, denoted by $\mathcal{E}(G)$, is obtained from the distance matrix of $G$ by keeping each entry that is the largest in its row or the largest in its column, and replacing all other entries by $0$. The eigenvalues of $\mathcal{E}(G)$ are called the $\mathcal{E}$-eigenvalues of $G$. In this article, we consider the eccentricity matrix of unicyclic graphs and study its various spectral properties. First, we give two sufficient conditions for the irreducibility of the eccentricity matrix of a connected graph, which generalize some previously known results. Then, we show that the eccentricity matrix of every unicyclic graph of girth $3$, $5$ or $7$ is irreducible and provide a unicyclic graph whose eccentricity matrix is reducible for every odd girth $g\ge 9$. On the other hand, we also provide a class of unicyclic graphs of odd girth, whose eccentricity matrices are always irreducible. Additionally, we find the inertia of eccentricity matrices of unicyclic graphs in which the trees attached to the cycle are nontrivial and have equal heights. Moreover, we characterize the graphs in this class whose E-eigenvalues are symmetric about the origin. Finally, we obtain necessary conditions for the invertibility of the eccentricity matrix of a unicyclic graph.

title: On unique realisations of graphs under symmetry constraints
text: On unique realisations of graphs under symmetry constraints. Global rigidity asks whether a realisation of a graph is uniquely determined, up to Euclidean congruence, by its edge lengths. In this paper, we study global rigidity of bar-joint frameworks under finite point-group symmetry constraints. A framework is called forced-symmetric globally rigid in $d$-space if every realisation of the graph in $\mathbb R^d$ with the same edge lengths and the same prescribed symmetry is congruent to it. We establish symmetric extensions of two fundamental results on global rigidity. Our first result extends Hendrickson's necessary condition to the forced-symmetric setting. For symmetry-generic frameworks with an arbitrary finite point group acting freely on the vertices and with at least $d+2$ vertex orbits, we prove that forced-symmetric global rigidity implies forced-symmetric redundant rigidity. Our second result extends the classical characterisation of generic global rigidity for body-bar frameworks due to Connelly, Jordán and Whiteley. For the symmetric body-bar model considered here, we show that forced-symmetric global rigidity is a generic property and obtain a combinatorial characterisation in every dimension.

title: The centre of mass of the primes and a reflection of Chebyshev's bias
text: The centre of mass of the primes and a reflection of Chebyshev's bias. For $x\ge2$ we place a unit mass at $\log p$ for each prime $p\le x$, and let $D(x)$ be the distance from the centre of mass of this system to $\log x$; thus $D(p_n)=\log(p_n/G_n)$, where $G_n$ is the geometric mean of the first $n$ primes. Let $D_0(x)$ be the distance obtained when $π$ is replaced by $\mathrm{Li}(x)=\int_2^x dt/\log t$. We prove that $D(x)-D_0(x)\ll x^{Θ-1+\varepsilon}$, where $Θ$ is the supremum of the real parts of the zeros of $ζ(s)$, and that the exponent cannot be lowered; in particular, the Riemann hypothesis is equivalent to $\log(p_n/G_n)=D_0(p_n)+O_\varepsilon(p_n^{-1/2+\varepsilon})$ for every $\varepsilon>0$. Under the Riemann hypothesis we prove a pointwise mirror theorem: for large $x$ the centre of mass lies to the left of its predicted position only when $π(x) \mathrm{li}(x)$, although for large $x$ the two sets are disjoint. We prove analogues for primes in arithmetic progressions, for the higher moments of the system, and, under a linear independence hypothesis, for $\mathbb{F}_q[T]$, where the biases of even and odd degrees are interchanged.

title: The Min-Cut Formulation of Ollivier-Ricci Curvature
text: The Min-Cut Formulation of Ollivier-Ricci Curvature. Computing Ollivier-Ricci curvature normally requires a local distance matrix and a linear program per edge, prompting workarounds based on entropic regularization or combinatorial proxies. We show that exact curvature needs neither. For any one-step measures, the Kantorovich dual has an integral three-level optimum, reducing each edge to one minimum s-t cut on a distance-free network linear in the read adjacency lists. This solves instances requiring quadratically many distance queries in linear time, while a converse reduction shows that no exact algorithm can beat bipartite matching. Our solver is a median 6 times (up to 506 times) faster than distance construction plus $\mathtt{POT}$'s C++ simplex, 441 times faster than $\mathtt{GraphRicciCurvature}$, and 23 times faster than graph min-cost flow. Even given the distances, Sinkhorn iterations at $\mathtt{GraphRicciCurvature}$'s regularization are a median 12 times slower, and combinatorial proxies alter edge rankings, missing the bulk of the most negatively curved ones.

title: Global Weak Solutions and Non-Formation of Vacuum States for Compressible Navier--Stokes--Korteweg Equations
text: Global Weak Solutions and Non-Formation of Vacuum States for Compressible Navier--Stokes--Korteweg Equations. A long-standing open problem in the mathematical theory of M-D fluid dynamics in viscous compressible flow is whether vacuum can form in finite time from initial data with density bounded away from zero. The underlying assumption in the derivation of systems of Navier--Stokes type from physical principles is that the fluid is non-dilute and can be described as a continuum. A negative answer to this problem would support the self-consistency of the continuum assumption for the Navier--Stokes-type models. This issue is particularly important when the viscosity coefficients are constant, since, from a physical standpoint, it is unclear how to meaningfully define the fluid velocity in vacuum regions, which in turn makes it difficult to interpret the associated viscous stresses. In this paper, for the barotropic compressible fluid with capillary effects, when the coefficients of viscosity and capillarity are all constants, we establish the global existence of weak solutions of the Cauchy problem for the corresponding Navier--Stokes--Korteweg equations with initial data that are large, radially symmetric, and away from the vacuum in two and three spatial dimensions. The failure of the well-known BD entropy estimate poses a substantial challenge to establishing this existence theory. Moreover, we rule out finite-time vacuum formation for the 2-D radially symmetric weak solutions constructed here. This extends, for the first time, the well-known Hoff--Smoller non-vacuum-formation theory (Commun. Math. Phys. 2001) from 1-D compressible Navier--Stokes equations with constant viscosity coefficients to 2-D radially symmetric flows with capillarity.

title: Integral Means of Fibonacci Numbers: Divisibility, Density, and Arithmetic Structure
text: Integral Means of Fibonacci Numbers: Divisibility, Density, and Arithmetic Structure. Motivated by recent works of Fatehizadeh, Yaqubi, Flynn-Connolly, Luca and Marques on the arithmetic mean of Fibonacci numbers, we study divisibility properties of sums of Fibonacci numbers whose indices form arithmetic progressions. We show that infinitely many even and odd $n$ divide such sums, and also the corresponding sums of squares and cubes, and we find all $n$ for which the geometric and harmonic means of $F_1,\ldots,F_n$ are integers. Further, we study the set $\mathcal{A}$ of integers $n\geq2$ for which the arithmetic mean of $F_1,\ldots,F_n$ is an integer. We show that $\mathcal{A}$ is both rich and sparse: it contains arbitrarily long arithmetic progressions and does not contain odd prime powers, yet $\#\{n\leq x: n\in\mathcal{A}\}\ll x/\sqrt{\log x}$. This density-zero bound holds more generally for every set $\{n: n\mid\sum_{i=0}^{n-1}F_{r+id}\}$. We also establish necessary conditions for three consecutive integral means (a question of Luca and Marques).

title: Counting tree-child and reticulation visible networks
text: Counting tree-child and reticulation visible networks. For tree-child networks with $n$ leaves and $k$ reticulations, we identify an entire critical scaling function at $k=x\sqrt n$ and its first uniform correction. The function is a Gaussian factor times the Laplace transform of Brownian excursion area. An exact coefficient integral then yields the explicit amplitude $π\Ai'(a_1)$ for the maximal-reticulation count, where $a_1$ is the largest negative Airy zero, together with three logarithmic corrections. A summable defect expansion transfers these results to the total number of tree-child networks. For reticulation-visible networks, we construct an exact weighted refinement over maximal tree-child networks. The total defect from $3n-3$ reticulations splits into a skeleton defect, an arity excess, and an ordinary-leaf count. The skeleton defect has a uniformly bounded exponential moment, and the full partition function differs from its maximal-skeleton sector by a bounded factor, smaller than $30$ at activity one. A positive algebraic kernel and an explicitly solved variational problem give the pressure with logarithmic error $O(n^{2/3}\log^{2/3}n)$. This determines the total exponential growth, the location of every mode, a full large-deviation principle, and limiting structural densities. At activity $z=t/n$ with fixed $t>0$, we also prove a $\operatorname{Poisson}(19t/4)$ limit and coefficient asymptotics uniform for defects $q=o(n^{1/3})$.

title: Trace-defined double covers of the $S_3$-involution graph of $PSL_2(2^n)$
text: Trace-defined double covers of the $S_3$-involution graph of $PSL_2(2^n)$. For $q=2^n\ge 4$, we construct a family of Deza double covers $Γ(q,ξ)$ of the $S_3$-involution graph of $PSL_2(q)$, parametrized by $ξ\in\mathbb F_q^*$. We show that each resulting cover is connected, arc-transitive and amply regular with parameters $(2(q^2-1),q,Tr(ξ),1)$, where $Tr$ denotes the absolute trace. We also show that the trace-one covers are antipodal of diameter $5$ and girth $3$, whereas the trace-zero covers are non-antipodal of diameter $3$ and girth $5$. For $q=4$, these cases yield the well-known icosidodecahedral and dodecadodecahedral graphs, respectively. Then we determine the distance distributions and full automorphism groups of the covers and prove that, for fixed $q$, two covers are isomorphic if and only if their defining parameters lie in the same Frobenius orbit. We also express the Ramanujan property of a cover in terms of the spectral norm of a signed adjacency matrix of the base graph.

title: Topological insulators on site-eliminated, projected, and patterned fractal lattices
text: Topological insulators on site-eliminated, projected, and patterned fractal lattices. Identifying fractal lattices of fractional (Hausdorff) dimension as geometric descendants of parent crystals, we showcase the successful realization of canonical topological insulators in one-, two-, and three-dimensional crystals on their self-similar descents using three complementary approaches, starting from lattice-regularized models in integer dimensions. (a) In the first approach, we construct the fractal Hamiltonian by removing all parent-lattice sites that do not belong to such a network (method of site elimination). (b) In the second one, we integrate or project out the same set of sites to obtain an effective Hamiltonian for the fractal lattice (method of projection or renormalization). (c) In the third approach, we retain the parent-crystal lattice intact but spatially pattern the on-site mass parameter, which controls the topology of the parent insulating system, such that it assumes two topologically distinct values on the fractal network and its complement (patterned fractal lattices). By numerically diagonalizing the resulting Hamiltonians and computing appropriate topological invariants or local markers, corroborating the bulk-boundary correspondence through gapless modes at outer or inner boundaries, we establish Su-Schrieffer-Heeger topology on the Cantor set using all three approaches, Haldane topology on the hexaflake [using (a) and (b)] and Qi-Wu-Zhang topology on the Sierpiński carpet [using (c)], and strong $Z_2$ topological insulating phases on the tiled Menger sponge from methods (a), (b), and (c). These findings complement and substantially extend the previously reported realization of Qi-Wu-Zhang topology on the Sierpiński carpet using methods (a) and (b) [Phys. Rev. B 110, L241302 (2024)].

title: VENUS: A Census of Strong Lensing in a 60-Cluster JWST Survey
text: VENUS: A Census of Strong Lensing in a 60-Cluster JWST Survey. We present strong-lensing models for the 57 galaxy clusters observed in Cycle 4 out of the 60 targeted by the JWST Vast Exploration for Nascent, Unexplored Sources (VENUS) program. Models for the remaining three clusters will be incorporated after their observations. The dataset comprises 5013 individual images, corresponding to 1733 multiply-imaged systems, of which 912 have spectroscopic redshift measurements and 227 are newly identified. Using this new wealth of observations, we construct parametric lens models with our $\mathtt{AstroLensPy}$ software, reproducing the observed image positions with an average image-plane precision $Δ_{\rm RMS}$ of $0.54''$. With a total imaging area of $576$ arcmin$^2$, VENUS offers the largest homogeneous set of cluster strong-lensing models to date. The clusters yield a combined area of $191$ arcmin$^{2}$ magnified by $|μ|\geq3$ for a source $z_s=10$, for example, establishing the VENUS fields as a premier survey for high-redshift studies. Among our sample, the clusters MACS J0717.5+3745, RXC J0600.1-2007 and PLCK G287.0+32.9 display the largest Einstein radii ($\geq 60''$) and magnified areas ($\mathcal{A}_{z_s=10}^{|μ|\geq3} \geq 9$ arcmin$^2$) for a source $z_s=10$, and therefore constitute the most potent gravitational telescopes known to date. Finally, leveraging the statistical power of the sample, we derive scaling relations between various lensing observables (Einstein radius, magnified area, projected mass) and the SZ/X-ray-inferred cluster mass, $M_{500,c}$.

title: Prospects and limitations of adaptive variational quantum algorithms for lattice field theories: a case study in 2+1 dimensions
text: Prospects and limitations of adaptive variational quantum algorithms for lattice field theories: a case study in 2+1 dimensions. The variational quantum algorithm ADAPT-VQE has previously been used to prepare the vacuum of lattice gauge theories in $1+1D$. In this paper, we study whether it extends to higher dimensions. We identify two general limitations of ADAPT-VQE. First, if the qubit Hamiltonian and the initial state are real, i.e., invariant under qubit-level time-reversal, all real-valued pool operators have vanishing gradients and are never selected. Second, the algorithm can converge to excited eigenstates. We illustrate both limitations, also providing examples from literature, and present a first application of ADAPT-VQE to a lattice field theory in $2+1D$, namely free Wilson fermions, where both obstacles occur. Adding charge conjugation symmetry to the operator pool improves the results, and combining different pools with suitable initial states recovers the ground and first excited states over the full mass range. These findings give practical guidelines for applying ADAPT-VQE to lattice field theories beyond $1+1D$.

title: Classical algorithms for sparse random Hamiltonians via free probability
text: Classical algorithms for sparse random Hamiltonians via free probability. The search for quantum advantage in average-case problems is a pressing open question in physics and computer science. The widest conjectured example of such an advantage is in simulation of quantum many-body systems, where sign problems and entanglement growth cause the breakdown of many classical methods. Nonetheless, theoretical evidence for or against such an advantage remains scarce. Here, we investigate this in sparse random non-local Hamiltonians. We design a classical algorithm for such Hamiltonians that enables accurate computation of spectral fluctuations, thermal values, and time-ordered and out-of-time-order correlation functions. For any subexponential precision $\varepsilon$, our algorithm runs in time $(1/\varepsilon)^{2+o(1)}$, nearly identical to a quantum simulation. Crucially, this applies even at late evolution times, low temperatures, and near critical points, where existing classical methods require exponential time. Rather than directly simulating a quantum state or operator, our algorithm first computes the model's mean behavior and then a short hierarchy of instance-dependent corrections. These corrections predict long-time behavior based on short-time data using free probability theory.

title: Scalar perturbations in extremal Reissner-Nordström geometry: new methods at work
text: Scalar perturbations in extremal Reissner-Nordström geometry: new methods at work. We study scalar radiation emitted by a particle moving along a circular orbit around a four-dimensional extremal Reissner-Nordström black hole. In particular, we calculate the energy fluxes carried by scalar waves to infinity and across the event horizon, as well as the scalar self-force acting on the particle, and express all these quantities as post-Newtonian expansions. Our results for the energy fluxes are in agreement with previous numerical findings in the literature. To solve the radial wave equation, we employ and test two distinct analytic approaches: the first is the so-called \textit{kink method}, a novel alternative stemming from quantum integrability and the second is the Mano-Suzuki-Takasugi method. The perfect agreement of the results highlights the potential of the kink method as a complementary tool for studying wave propagation in black-hole spacetimes.

title: Anomalies and the Berry Phase: From $π^0\toγγ$ to the geometry of the fermion vacuum
text: Anomalies and the Berry Phase: From $π^0\toγγ$ to the geometry of the fermion vacuum. We review the chiral anomaly from a historical perspective, from the $π^0\toγγ$ puzzle and the work of Adler, Bell and Jackiw, to the Wess-Zumino-Witten (WZW) term. We then describe how the WZW term was motivated from quantum chromodynamics in 1983-85. Integrating out the non-Abelian gauge fields, that have a gapped spectrum, gives a Nambu-Jona-Lasinio type theory of quarks, and integrating out the quarks, which are gapped by chiral symmetry breaking, gives the WZW model. The fermion determinant splits into a regulator-dependent modulus, which gives the dynamics of mesons, and a universal phase, which is fixed by the anomaly and is the WZW term. Restricted to the collective coordinates of the baryon soliton, the WZW term imposes a U(1) constraint that makes the baryon wave functions monopole harmonics and fixes their spin, statistics and flavour multiplets. We then explain that this phase is a Berry phase: the Schwinger terms of current algebra are the curvature of a U(1) connection on the space of chiral field configurations, and the WZW term is its holonomy, which we call a Berry-Wilson loop. In 1+1 dimensions we write the connection explicitly in terms of Euler angles, exhibiting a Dirac monopole whose quantised charge is the level of the current algebra.

title: Robust growth of $α$-tantalum on sapphire at room temperature using atomically thin titanium seed layer
text: Robust growth of $α$-tantalum on sapphire at room temperature using atomically thin titanium seed layer. Tantalum (Ta) based superconducting circuits have attracted attention for their low microwave loss. However, reproducible growth of high-quality $α$-phase Ta films remains challenging because film properties are highly sensitive to growth conditions. We present a robust, room-temperature route for $α$-Ta growth on sapphire substrates using an ultrathin Ti seed layer, which significantly widens the accessible deposition parameter space. We compare this approach to Ta films grown at high temperature without a seed layer and at room temperature with a Nb seed. We assess films using structural and surface characterization and quantify microwave loss with coplanar-waveguide (CPW) resonators measured in the quantum regime. We obtain two-level-system (TLS)-limited quality factors comparable to the state of the art for Ta-on-sapphire CPW resonators with similar geometries. In addition, temperature-dependent measurements reveal that high-temperature-grown films and films subjected to extended buffered-oxide etch treatment exhibit additional temperature activated loss, highlighting the role of growth route and post-processing in microwave performance. Our results establish ultrathin seed-layer engineering as a reliable alternative route to reproducible, low-loss $α$-Ta films and motivate closer study of the interfacial mechanisms that govern Ta phase formation.

title: CANON: Agent-Assisted Construction of Canonical Differential Equations for Feynman Integrals
text: CANON: Agent-Assisted Construction of Canonical Differential Equations for Feynman Integrals. The construction of canonical basis is an important procedure in the calculation of multi-loop Feynman integrals via the canonical differential equation methods. Currently, there are various different methods for this purpose. Among them, no single method is universally applicable. Thus, obtaining a valid basis often requires repeated attempts and verification. In this paper, we present CANON, an agent-assisted framework designed to make this search-and-verification process more convenient and more efficient. In this workflow, the agent selects methods and calls the corresponding tools to revise the basis proposal or the associated differential-equation system. Independent programs then verify whether the agent's result is valid and ask the agent to retry if verification fails. This framework contains a specific state-management tool to supports long-range basis searching works which requires multiple sub-agents. Its modular architecture enables future extensions to the framework itself. In this paper, we demonstrate this framework by applying it to some two-loop and three-loop integral families.

title: Hesperos & Eosphoros: A Coupled Differentiable Forced-Photometry Operator and Forward Model for SPHEREx Spectrophotometry
text: Hesperos & Eosphoros: A Coupled Differentiable Forced-Photometry Operator and Forward Model for SPHEREx Spectrophotometry.
