title: Andres Odhiambo
text: Andres Odhiambo Omondi (born 12 October 2007) also known as Andreas Odhiambo is a Kenyan professional footballer who plays as a midfielder for Swedish side Enköpings SK and the Kenya under-23 national team. Career Andres came through the FKF Centre of Excellence programme and went on to feature for all Kenya junior sides including the U15, U17, U18, U20, and now the U23 side. In November 2026, he scored an 83rd-minute winner as Kenya U23 beat Ivory Coast 2–1 in the first leg of their 2027 U-23 AFCON qualifier at Nyayo National Stadium. Kenya lost the return leg 2–0 in Abidjan on 17 November and were eliminated 3–2 on aggregate. Andres was part of the Kenya U20 that qualified for the 2025 U-20 Africa Cup of Nations after Kenya U20 qualified for the CECAFA U20 Championship final in Tanzania in December 2024. He went on to feature at the tournament held in Cairo, Egypt in May 2025 and featured in all three group matches against Morocco, Tunisia and Nigeria. Andres' Kenyan Premier League journey started out with the youth side of Kenyan Premier League team Kariobangi Sharks then graduated to the senior side in February 2024. He became the youngest-ever FKF Premier League goalscorer at 16 years, 11 months and 10 days old. Two years later, in February 2026, he moved abroad to join Swedish side Enköpings SK. In March 2025, he was named in the provisional squad for the senior Kenya national team by head coach Benny McCarthy for preparations ahead of two World Cup qualifiers against Gabon and Gambia, but did not make the final squad. In early April 2025, he unsuccessfully tried out with Norwegian side Sarpsborg 08 FF. In the Swedish Cup, he played the full match and assisted the opener as Enköping beat Rågsveds IF 2–0 in the first round on 17 June 2026. In the second round on 19 August 2026, he scored Enköping's goal in a 1–2 home loss to Västerås SK. Enköping finished second in Ettan Norra in 2026 with 55 points and reached the Superettan promotion play-off against Örebro SK. Odhiambo started the first leg at home on 21 November 2026, which Enköping lost 2–4, and was substituted off in the 75th minute.

title: 1020 incident
text: The 1020 incident (Burmese: ၁၀၂၀ ဖြစ်စဉ်), officially referred to by the Chinese government as the "10·20" shooting incident (Chinese: “10·20”枪击案), is an incident that occurred on 20 October 2023, in the Kokang Self-Administered Zone of Myanmar, in which a Chinese citizen suspected of being involved in telecom fraud was killed. Multiple media reports on the details of the incident differed. The general situation was that hundreds of Chinese citizens were trapped in the Wohushanzhuang Telecom Fraud Park controlled by the Ming Xuechang family and engaged in telecom fraud. Under pressure from China's anti-telecom fraud campaign, the militia under the Ming family transferred Chinese telecom fraud personnel to other places. During the transfer, some people tried to escape. Chinese undercover police officers who were assisting the Chinese citizens revealed their identities and tried to stop the Ming family militia from transferring, but were killed instead. Several Chinese citizens died in the incident. Myanmar's independent media Myanmar Now quoted sources from the Myanmar state media's military government to confirm the incident. The incident was officially confirmed by China on 30 December 2024. However, the casualties were different from those previously reported by the media, and it was denied that any Chinese police officers were killed or injured. Many media outlets regarded it as the fuse of the Operation 1027. Background The Kokang Self-Administered Zone is part of Shan State in Myanmar and was controlled by the Myanmar National Democratic Alliance Army (MNDAA) before the 2009 Kokang incident. The MNDAA is an ethnic armed organization established by Pheung Kya-shin in 1989. After Pheung withdrew from the peace talks between the Communist Party of Burma and the military government, he and his subordinates established the MNDAA and implemented autonomy in Kokang. In 2009, the MNDAA experienced internal strife, and Pheung was betrayed by some of his subordinates. They cooperated with the Tatmadaw to drive the MNDAA out of the Kokang region. They were known as the Four Families of Kokang, namely Bai Suocheng, Wei Chaoren, Liu Guoxi and Liu Zhengxiang (Liu Abao). The Ming Xuechang family rose to prominence afterward, becoming a rising star outside the Four Families, and had close ties with the Four Families. With the support of the military junta, the Four Families and the Ming Xuechang family controlled the politics, economy and military of the Kokang region and engaged in various illegal activities such as drug trafficking, smuggling, gambling and telecommunications fraud. Telecom fraud is one of the main sources of income for the four major families, from which they make huge profits, and it is also the main source of their conflict with China. These fraud groups are mainly composed of Chinese nationals who use various means, such as telephone, internet or social media, to defraud victims in China of their money. These fraudsters are usually recruited by the four major families with high salaries or other inducements, but once they arrive in the Kokang region, they are deprived of their freedom and forced to work under strict surveillance, and cannot leave or contact the outside world at will. Once they are found to have the intention to escape or resist, they will be severely punished, or even killed. The United States Institute of Peace reported that the Chinese authorities "deliberately stood by" on the issue of telecom fraud. However, starting in the summer of 2023, the Chinese authorities allowed Chinese films on the subject of telecom fraud in northern Myanmar, including No More Bets, Tainted Love and Lost in the Stars, to be released, and the films grossed more than $1 billion. These films conveyed the message that "Chinese citizens can only be safe in Southeast Asia with China’s help". By mid-September 2023, China took unilateral action to exert unprecedented pressure on Shan State and Wa State. The incident In Octobe

title: Battle of Gabes (741)
text: The Battle of Gabes was a battle fought between the Berbers led by Ukkasha and the Umayyads who were led by Maslama ibn Sawada in the year 741. The battle was fought in the area of Gabes in present-day Tunisia. Background It had been around two years since the war between the Berbers and the Umayyads began. The Berber Revolt had been so far successful for the Berbers especially after their defeat of the Umayyads in the Tangier expedition (740) and the Battle of The Nobles, where they managed to later isolate the Umayyad armies into Ceuta and begin the Siege of Ceuta. By then most of Northwest Africa had been retaken by the Berbers, with the Berber Revolution reaching areas such as present day Tunisia and Libya. Battle Ukkasha who was in Gabes had rebelled against the Umayyads after Kulthum ibn Iyad al-Qushayri had left to attack the Berbers. Maslama ibn Sawada who was the Umayyad responsible for Kairouan went out with an Umayyad army to attack Ukkasha in Gabes. However, the Umayyads were defeated and most of the Umayyads were killed. Maslama ibn Sawada returned to Kairouan after his defeat, and Maslama ordered for Kairouan to be fortified under the leadership of Saeed ibn Bajra al-Ghassani. Aftermath Ukkasha would then go to Algeria where he would encounter the other Berber commander Al-Hawwari in the Ziban region of present-day Algeria, both decided to split apart and take different paths back into Tunisia. Ukkasha took a valley route while Al-Hawwari marched through the Awras Mountains.

title: Arrowhead (album)
text: Arrowhead is a studio album by American musician Dominick Fernow under the pseudonym Prurient. It was released on July 28, 2008, through Editions Mego. It received universal acclaim from critics. Background Dominick Fernow, better known as Prurient, is an American musician originally from Wisconsin. Arrowhead was recorded in winter 2004 in Providence, Rhode Island, and was finalized in winter 2005 in New York City, New York. The album consists of three tracks ("Sternum", "Ribcage", and "Lungs"), clocking in at 30 minutes. It features a guest appearance from Kris Lapke. The album was released on July 28, 2008, through Editions Mego. Critical reception According to the review aggregator Metacritic, Arrowhead received "universal acclaim" based on a weighted average score of 83 out of 100 from 5 critic scores. François Couture of AllMusic wrote, "Without actually marking a new direction, Arrowhead does open up Prurient's music to a spatial dimension hitherto unsuspected." He added, "It should still satisfy noise fans, but amateurs of sound art will also find it welcoming." Grayson Currin of Pitchfork stated, "Listen for the control Fernow wields over his electronics as he grapples with the tone, letting it slide into chaos only to bring it back under his hand." He added, "There's a violent, lacerating ebb-and-flow to this work that's as nauseating as it is enrapturing." Track listing Personnel Credits adapted from liner notes. title: 2025 Venezuelan regional elections
text: Regional elections were held in Venezuela on 25 May 2025 to elect the governors of the country's 24 claimed states and members of their respective state legislative councils. The elections were held concurrently with the parliamentary election, in which members of the National Assembly for the 2026–2031 term were chosen. The elections took place against a backdrop of political crisis, following the disputed 2024 presidential election—an event that sparked protests against the results announced by the National Electoral Council (CNE). Tensions continued into early January 2025, with demonstrations opposing the inauguration of Nicolás Maduro and protesting the CNE’s lack of transparency in releasing the full election results—a concern echoed by international observers—alongside the initiation of UN investigations into electoral fraud. In the days leading up to the elections, the Venezuelan government carried out a wave of arrests, detaining more than 70 individuals—including politicians, activists, journalists, and lawyers—on accusations of involvement in conspiracies. The electoral process was marked by low nationwide turnout and a heavy presence of state security forces. While the CNE claimed a turnout of 42.63%, the opposition’s Comando con Venezuela stated that turnout was only 12.56%. Furthermore, irregularities arose during the announcement of the results, as the reported turnout percentage did not align with the number of voters indicated in the initial electoral bulletin. Background On 28 July 2024, presidential elections were held, in which the National Electoral Council proclaimed Nicolás Maduro president-elect with 51.95% of the vote. The elections were deemed neither free nor fair, as they took place in a context where the government controlled all branches of the State while repressing the political opposition. For its part, the opposition rejected these figures, asserting that Edmundo González had won with 67.05% of the vote, based on the electoral records (tally sheets) in their possession. Candidates Enrique Márquez, Claudio Fermín, and Antonio Ecarri also demanded the publication of the official vote tally sheets. Several countries expressed their rejection of the results, pointed to irregularities, and called for the publication of the vote tally sheets. Call for Elections On November 9, 2024, President Nicolás Maduro raised the possibility of holding regional elections in separate stages—first for mayors, then for governors, and subsequently for the Parliament. "It would seem that the best approach would be to hold separate elections: first mayors, then governors, and then the Parliament—though that is just my opinion; it is one perspective among many in the debate," he stated. On January 15, 2025, the National Assembly began organizing a working group involving various sectors, including a minority opposition aligned with the ruling party (consisting largely of political parties that have been subject to judicial intervention). Notably absent from these consultative meetings were the major opposition factions, which are organized under the Unitary Platform. Despite this absence, the ruling party continued discussions to develop proposals and potential dates, which were to be submitted to the CNE to establish an electoral calendar for the upcoming regional and parliamentary elections. Electoral Abstention On January 19, 2025, María Corina Machado, the opposition leader from the Unitary Platform, issued a message via social media calling for a boycott of the elections. She stated: "The elections took place on July 28 (2024). That day, the people made their choice... The result must be—and will be—respected. Until that result takes effect, participating in any kind of election is inappropriate. Going to vote time and again without the results being respected is not defending the vote; it is undermining the popular will." title: Gary Hill (American football)
text: Gary Harold Hill (born June 29, 1943 – August 9, 2026) was an American professional football player who was a defensive back for the Minnesota Vikings of the National Football League (NFL). He played college football for the USC Trojans. Early life Hill was born on June 29, 1943, in Los Angeles, California. He attended Rancho Alamitos High School in Garden Grove, California. College career Hill played college football for the USC Trojans from 1961 to 1964 and was a three-year letterman from 1962 to 1964. He had six rushes for 37 yards with one reception for 14 yards in 30 games. In 1964, he earned first-team All-Pacific Coast honors. Professional career After not being selected in the 1965 NFL draft, Hill signed with the Minnesota Vikings as an undrafted free agent. On August 9, he was waived. On August 12, Hill was signed to the taxi squad. On October 29, he was elevated to the active roster to play as a reserve safety and on special teams. During the 1965 season, Hill played in eight games. On August 30, 1966, he was waived by the Vikings. Personal life After his playing career ended, Hill served in the U.S. Army in Korea. He later worked as a financial advisor for Dean Witter Reynolds and Morgan Stanley. Hill died on August 9, 2026, in Huntington Beach, California. References

title: Abdel Fattah el-Shasha'i
text: Abdel Fattah Mahmoud el-Shasha'i (21 March 1890 – 11 November 1962) was an Egyptian Quran reciter. He studied Quran recitation and its rules in Tanta and the seven canonical readings at Al-Azhar in Cairo. He graduated from a teachers' training school in Qalyubia and taught at a religious school established by his father for three years. He began recording Quran recitations for Egyptian Radio in 1937 and was appointed as a reciter at the Sayyida Zainab Mosque in Cairo in 1940. He was known as the 'Emperor of Recitation' and as 'Abu al-Qurra' (Father of the Reciters). Early life and education Abdel Fattah el-Shasha'i was born on 21 March 1890 in the village of Sha'sha', in Ashmoun, Monufia Governorate. He memorised the Quran under his father Mahmoud Ibrahim el-Shasha'i, reportedly at the age of ten. In 1900, he moved to Tanta, where he studied Quran recitation and its rules (tajwid) under Ismail al-Shafi'i and various other teachers at Ahmad al-Badawi Mosque until 1905. He graduated from a teachers' training school in Qalyubiyya Governorate and subsequently taught for three years at a religious school established by his father. In 1916, el-Shasha'i began studying the seven canonical recitations in Al-Azhar in Cairo, under Muhammad Bayyumi and Ali Subay. Career El-Shasha'i formed a religious chanting (tawashih) troupe, whose members included the composer Zakariyya Ahmad before his fame. He arrived in Cairo in 1914 and settled in the Darb al-Ahmar neighbourhood. His fame spread after he recited on the closing night of the Mawlid of Imam Hussein, alongside the leading reciters of the era, including Muhammad Rifat, Ahmed Nada, Ali Mahmoud, al-Isawi and Muhammad Jadallah. From 1930 he left tawashih completely and devoted himself to Quran recitation, while continuing to pay monthly salaries to his former troupe members until their deaths. In the mid-1920s he founded an association to gather the reciters, and proposed a monthly religious concert broadcast on radio with the senior reciters, as a response to Umm Kulthum's monthly concerts. In 1936, el-Shasha'i recited the Quran at Abdeen Palace during King Fuad's funeral. He had earlier recited at the funerals of Saad Zaghloul and Adly Yakan. In 1937, he began recording the Quran recitation on Egyptian Radio, becoming the second radio reciter after Muhammad Rifat. He had initially refused to recite on the radio, considering it to be religiously impermissible. However, he changed his stance after receiving a fatwa from the Grand Imam of al-Azhar. After accepting the radio offer, he received an annual salary of 500 Egyptian pounds. In 1940, he was appointed as a reciter at the Sayyida Zainab Mosque in Cairo, and held this position until his death. He also served as reciter in Sayyida Nafisa Mosque. In 1948, during Hajj, he became the first Egyptian reciter to recite the Quran over loudspeakers at the Masjid al-Haram in Mecca, the Prophet's Mosque in Medina, and the Arafat stand. He also travelled to countries in the Arab and Muslim world, and recited in Iraq several times in the 1950s. He developed his own style of recitation, imitating no teacher, and no one could imitate him. Despite a weak build, his voice was powerful and impressive, and it grew more beautiful with age. He was disciplined in applying tajwid and a master at adjusting his voice to the meaning. Personal life El-Shasha'i had seven children, of whom only the youngest, Ibrahim, became a hafiz. His youngest son, Ibrahim el-Shasha'i, memorised the Quran and succeeded his father as a reciter at the Sayyida Zaynab Mosque, holding the position until his death on 9 June 1992. Death and legacy El-Shasha'i died on 11 November 1962 in Shubra, Cairo. He left behind numerous recordings of his recitations which continue to be broadcast. In 2025 his family gifted the Quran Radio dozens of rare recitations never broadcast before, saying they hold about 300 unbroadcast recitations to gift gradually to the National Media Authority. title: 2025 Delhi Republic Day parade
text: The 76th Delhi Republic Day Parade or the 2025 Delhi Republic Day Parade was held on 26 January 2025 at Kartavya Path, New Delhi. The ceremony was the main highlight of the national celebrations marking India's 76th Republic Day, featuring marching contingents of the Indian Armed Forces, tableaux from states and union territories, cultural performances, and a grand flypast by the Indian Air Force. The President of Indonesia, Prabowo Subianto, attended the event as the chief guest. The 76th Delhi Republic Day Parade featured contingents from the Indian Army, Indian Navy, Indian Air Force, Central Armed Police Forces, as well as various schools and cultural groups. It was the third Republic Day parade held during the presidency of Droupadi Murmu and showcased India's military capabilities, cultural diversity, and special presentations commemorating 75 years of the Constitution of India. Background India celebrates Republic Day annually on 26 January, commemorating the day in 1950 when the Constitution of India came into effect and India became a sovereign democratic republic. The Republic Day parade, held at Kartavya Path in New Delhi, is regarded as one of the country's most prestigious national events. It showcases the military capabilities of the Indian Armed Forces, cultural diversity, scientific achievements, and national unity. The 76th Delhi Republic Day Parade was held on 26 January 2025. The 2025 celebrations were particularly significant as they coincided with the 75th anniversary of the Constitution of India coming into effect. Accordingly, the ceremony placed special emphasis on constitutional values, democratic traditions, cultural heritage, and the vision of Viksit Bharat (Developed India). Extensive security arrangements, rehearsals, traffic management measures, and preparations by tableau and cultural groups were undertaken ahead of the parade. Contingents from the Indian Army, Indian Navy, Indian Air Force, and Central Armed Police Forces participated in the ceremony. In addition, tableaux from various states, union territories, and central ministries showcased India's cultural diversity, technological progress, and development. Cultural performances by school students and folk artists also added to the spectacle of the parade. The President of Indonesia, Prabowo Subianto, attended the ceremony as the chief guest. The parade concluded with the traditional flypast by the Indian Air Force, featuring various aircraft and helicopters. The event was regarded as an important symbol of India's military strength, cultural richness, and international friendship. References

title: 42nd Infantry Regiment (South Vietnam)
text: The 42nd Infantry Regiment was a unit under II Corps of the Army of Republic of Vietnam (ARVN). The regiment operated independently from mid-1965 till 1970 under the 24th Special Tactical Zone. Subsequently, it fought in the 22nd Infantry Division formation during the Second battle of Dak To in 1972, and was later disbanded along with the re-formed division during the Fall of Saigon in 1975. History On 22–23 February 1965, the regiment's 3rd Battalion, ran into an enemy force armed with AK-47s and RPG-2s between Dak To and the Cambodian border. Outclassed, the unit recoiled in disorder. The next day, the regimental commander, Lt. Col. Lại Văn Chu, personally led a second battalion in a counterattack that captured some of these new weapons. In the process, the South Vietnamese identified their foe as the PAVN 101st Regiment. During April–May 1965, II Corps commander, Maj. Gen. Nguyễn Hữu Có had detached the regiment from the 22nd Division to create the 24th Special Tactical Zone (24th STZ) - covering Kontum, Pleiku, and Phú Bổn provinces. On 7 July 1965, the PAVN captured Đăk Tô and rebuffed an attempt by the regiment to regain the post, killing its commander and seriously wounding his adviser. II Corps commander, Maj. Gen. Vĩnh Lộc appointed Col. Đàm Văn Quí to command the regiment. Bolstered by three additional battalions, Quí regained the town. From 2–21 June 1966, in Operation Hawthorne, the 1/42nd Battalion along with the 21st Ranger Battalion under the 24th STZ provided support to the US 2nd Battalion, 502nd Infantry Regiment fighting against the PAVN 24th Regiment near the village of Toumorong, Kontum province. From 6 April to 11 October 1967, the 42nd participated in Operation Francis Marion with the US 4th Infantry Division and 173rd Airborne Brigade against PAVN base areas in Pleiku, Darlac and Kontum provinces. Total PAVN losses were 1600 killed. On 17 June 1967, a battalion of the PAVN 24th Regiment, reinforced with a battalion of the 40th Artillery Regiment, attacked the 42nd HQ at Tân Cảnh Base Camp. In Operation Greeley early August, the 24th STZ airlifted a battalion of the 42nd and the entire 1st Airborne Task Force to the Dak Seang Camp. As these forces pushed westward into the rugged hills overlooking Dak Seang, they met a strongly entrenched and reinforced battalion of the PAVN 174th Regiment. After a fight lasting four days, with heavy air support called in by US advisers, the ARVN seized the position and drove the PAVN into Laos. The ARVN found 189 PAVN bodies, large quantities of ammunition and equipment, and a sophisticated regimental command post withtraining areas and an elaborate mock-up of the Camp. 1968 Tet Offensive 1972 Easter Offensive In early 1972, to counter the possible threat from the west, Lt. Gen. Ngô Du had deployed the regiment and the 47th Regiment to Tân Cảnh and Đắk Tô Base Camp, as well as two armored squadrons (14th and 19th) to Ben Het. 1975 Spring Offensive Before the Fall of Saigon, the regiment along with the 41st Regiment took part in the defense of Bến Lức / Tân An and Route 4 under the Capital Military District alongside local RF/PF and the 12th Regiment of the 7th Division. title: Andrew Sunyar
text: Andrew William Sunyar (1920 – May 22, 1986) was an American nuclear physicist who spent his career at Brookhaven National Laboratory. He is best known as a co-author, with Maurice Goldhaber and Lee Grodzins, of the Goldhaber experiment of late 1957, a tabletop measurement which showed that neutrinos emitted in orbital electron capture have negative helicity, meaning that they are left-handed. The result gave key support to the emerging view that the weak interaction is a single fundamental force. Sunyar's other work included a classification of nuclear isomers with Goldhaber that supported the nuclear shell model, some of the earliest applications of the Mössbauer effect to nuclear and solid-state measurements, and the leadership of Brookhaven's tandem Van de Graaff research group, which gained international recognition in heavy-ion physics. Early life and education Sunyar was born in 1920 in Henderson, Michigan and graduated from Albion College in 1942. He began graduate study at the University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign (UIUC), but the work was interrupted when he served as an officer in the United States Navy during World War II. After the war, he returned to Illinois and completed a doctorate in physics in 1949. His thesis concerned resonance absorption of slow neutrons in nuclei with the same number of protons and neutrons in the atomic nucleus. At UIUC, Sunyar was among the students of Maurice Goldhaber, who took part in Goldhaber's studies of short-lived nuclear isomers at the CP-3 reactor of Argonne National Laboratory. Career Sunyar joined Brookhaven National Laboratory immediately after receiving his doctorate and remained there for the rest of his life. He became co-leader of the laboratory's nuclear structure group and later led the tandem Van de Graaff research group, which, under his direction, became known worldwide for its heavy ion research. In the early 1950s, Sunyar turned to measuring the rates of nuclear transitions as a way of identifying and characterizing nuclear levels. He built one of the fastest coincidence timing systems of its day and used it to measure many nuclear lifetimes shorter than a nanosecond. He worked with most isomers that could be produced with the reactors and cyclotrons of the period. His systematic study of isomers led to a 1951 paper with Goldhaber. The authors reexamined earlier lifetime and energy relations, concluded that the spin changes inferred for slow electric transitions had been one unit too large, and found that most long-lived isomers were consistent with the shell model. They also assigned spins for a number of nuclei and observed that the first excited state of an even-even nucleus usually has spin 2 and even parity. After the discovery that parity is not conserved in beta decay, Sunyar, Goldhaber, and Grodzins used measurements of the helicities of photons and electrons to probe the nature of the beta-decay interaction. In 1957 the three reported evidence for circular polarization of bremsstrahlung produced by beta rays. Goldhaber experiment In October 1957, Goldhaber was asked to survey the question of neutrino helicity for a meeting of the American Physical Society that December at Stanford University. He conceived a method based on the europium isomer 152mEu, which decays by orbital electron capture to an excited state of samarium-152 that then emits a gamma ray. A combined analysis of the gamma ray's circular polarization and its resonant scattering reveals the helicity of the neutrino emitted in the capture. The scheme depended on the technique of resonance fluorescence, which Grodzins had recently demonstrated at Brookhaven. Sunyar and Grodzins carried out the measurement in Building 119 at Brookhaven. The experiment took about ten days, followed by roughly a month of checks, and the paper was submitted to Physical Review on December 11, 1957. title: 2021 WPT Menorca Open
text: The 2021 Menorca Open (officially 2021 World Padel Tour Estrella Damm Menorca Open) was the fourteenth tournament of the ninth season organized by World Padel Tour, the most prestigious padel circuit at the time. In the women's category, the first and third-ranked pairs reached the final. The first finalists were the world number ones, Alejandra Salazar and Gemma Triay, who defeated the fourth-seeded pair, Delfina Brea and Tamara Icardo, in the semi-finals. Their opponents were the newly formed third-ranked pair, Lucia Sainz and Marta Marrero, who had defeated their former partners and sixth-ranked pair, Bea González and Marta Ortega, in the semi-finals. In the decisive match, Gemma and Salazar defeated Marrero and Sainz in three sets, securing their seventh title of the season (and their fourth consecutive). With this victory, Salazar successfully defended the title she won in the previous edition, while Gemma claimed her first title on home soil. In the men's category, the top two ranked pairs reached the final, setting up a rematch of the previous tournament's final. The first finalists were the world number ones, Alejandro Galán and Juan Lebrón, who defeated the new number three-ranked pair, Agustín Tapia and Sanyo Gutiérrez, in the semi-finals. Their opponents were the second-ranked pair, Martín Di Nenno and Paquito Navarro, who eliminated Alejandro Ruiz and Franco Stupaczuk to reach their fourth consecutive final. In the decisive match, Galán and Lebrón defeated Di Nenno and Paquito in straight sets, securing their sixth title of the season and successfully defending the title they had won for the first time the previous year. title: 2021 WPT Lugo Open
text: The 2021 Lugo Open (officially 2021 World Padel Tour Trofeo Concello de Lugo Open) was the thirteenth tournament of the ninth season organized by World Padel Tour, the most prestigious padel circuit at the time. In the women's category, the first and fifth-ranked pairs reached the final, setting up a rematch of their encounter from the season's third tournament in Vigo. The first finalists were the world number ones, Alejandra Salazar and Gemma Triay, who defeated the fourth-ranked pair, Delfina Brea and Tamara Icardo, in the semi-finals. Their opponents were the fifth-ranked pair, Patricia Llaguno and Virginia Riera, who reached the final after defeating Aranzazu Osoro and Victoria Iglesias in the semi-finals. In the decisive match, Gemma and Salazar defeated Iglesias and Osoro in straight sets, securing their sixth title of the season and the pair's first in Lugo (the second for Salazar who had already won in 2018). In the men's category, the first and fourth-ranked pairs both reached the final for the first time this season. The first finalists were the world number ones, Alejandro Galán and Juan Lebrón, who defeated Alejandro Arroyo and Arturo Coello in the semi-finals. Their opponents were the fourth-ranked pair, Martín Di Nenno and Paquito Navarro, who eliminated Javier Rico and Momo González to reach the final. In the decisive match, Galán and Lebrón defeated Di Nenno and Paquito in three sets, securing their fifth title of the season. With this victory, Galán successfully defended the title he had won in the previous edition (in 2018), while Lebrón claimed his first title in Lugo. Relevant Data Pairs split up and new partners In the women's category, Marta Marrero and Marta Ortega—who had finished 2019 as the world number ones and reunited towards the end of 2020—announced their split following this tournament, as did the third-ranked pair, Bea González and Lucía Sainz. Bea would go on to reunite with the Marta she had partnered with in 2020, while Lucía would join forces with Marta Marrero. On the men's side, prior to the start of the tournament, the second-ranked pair of the year and the second most successful in terms of tournament won, Fernando Belasteguín and Sanyo Gutiérrez, announced that they would be playing their final tournament together. Belasteguín's decision was reportedly prompted by poor results in the last three tournaments. Consequently, the third-ranked pair, Agustín Tapia and Pablo Lima, also decided to part ways, with Tapia choosing to end his partnership with Lima to team up with Sanyo Gutiérrez, marking the fourth time he has played alongside a former world number one, having previously partnered with Juan Martín Díaz, Belasteguín, and Lima. Meanwhile, Belasteguín joined forces with Arturo Coello, while Lima teamed up with Javi Ruiz. title: Aletta Lorentz-Kaiser
text: Aletta Catharina Lorentz-Kaiser (Amsterdam, 15 April 1858 - 1 October 1931) was a Dutch feminist. She was the youngest daughter of Johanna Buisman and Johan Willem Kaiser, a professor at the Rijksakademie van Beeldende Kunsten and director of the Rijksmuseum. She was also the niece of Dutch astronomer Frederik Kaiser. In 1881, Aletta Kaiser married the physcist Hendrik Lorentz and the couple lived in Leiden. They had four children, of whom the youngest son died in his first year. Their oldest daughter was the physicist Geertruida de Haas-Lorentz. Activism for children In 1885, Lorentz-Kaiser was approached by the textile manufacturer C. H. Krantz and his wife about starting a kinderbewaarplaats. The kinderbewaarplaats was an early form of child care meant for the children of working or sick mothers. Loretnz became the secretary of the Association for the Care of Small Children. She left the board of this association in 1893. In 1904 she joined a board for the construction of a public playground meant for poorer children and open to all children regardless of religious affiliation. Women's rights activism In 1900 the Leiden branch of the Vereeniging voor Vrouwenkiesrecht was established and Lorentz-Kaiser was invited to join its board. In addition to her administrative duties, she supported the Association by visiting university professors to encourage them to engage with the women's movement. Aletta Lorentz-Kaiser also joined the Vereniging Onderlinge Vrouwenbescherming (Association for Mutual Protection of Women) and served on its board in 1902. This organization provided assistance to single mothers. In 1907, Lorentz-Kaiser was part of a splinter group of members of the a group of members broke away from the Vereeniging voor Vrouwenkiesrecht to form the more moderate Nederlandsche Bond voor Vrouwenkiesrecht. This new organization allowed men to serve on its board and opposed some of the tactics employed by suffragettes. Lorentz-Kaiser became vice-chair (and later chair) of the Leiden branch's executive board, with responsibility for the propaganda portfolio. She also continued her efforts to engage university professors and played a role in the establishment of several other local branches. In 1911 Lorentz-Kaiser stepped down from her administrative positions in Leiden because in 1912 her husband took up a new position and the couple moved to Haarlem. In 1913 she served on the board of the Association for the Improvement of the Social and Legal Status of Women in the Netherlands. Hendrik Lorentz died in 1928 and Aletta Lorentz-Kaiser died in 1931. Sources Agnes van Steen, 'Vol moed en blakende van ijver', Aletta Lorentz-Kaiser en de vrouwenbeweging in Leiden (1881-1912) in Jaarboek Dirk van Eck, 2011, p.125-166 noord-hollandsarchief.nl Archief 364 Lorentz, prof. dr. H.A., te Haarlem, 1. Hendrik Antoon Lorentz, Huwelijk en gezin en 2. Aletta Catharina Kaiser Kox, A.J.: Hendrik Antoon Lorentz. title: Christer Norström
text: Christer Norström, born in 1952, is a Swedish social anthropologist whose research has focused on hunter-gatherer societies, indigenous peoples, environmental movements, and rural livelihoods in South India. He is known for his ethnographic work among the Paliyan people of the Palani Hills (Palni Hills) in the state of Tamil Nadu. Beyond his work on the Paliyans, Norström has researched food production, food security, and agricultural change in South India, as well as the history and experiences of environmental activists in the region. Borneo 1981-1982 In 1981 before Norström had started his profession as social anthropologist, he did a journey to the Malaysian part of Borneo with a friend and visited Sarawak and Sabah. There is a collection of photographs from this journey in the Museum of Ethnography in Stockholm. In an interview he says that the experience sparked a lasting interest in indigenous societies and cultural diversity and influenced his decision to pursue studies in social anthropology. Work among the Paliyan Norström's doctoral dissertation,"They Call for Us": Strategies for Securing Autonomy among the Paliyans, Hunter-Gatherers of the Palni Hills, South India was based on fieldwork conducted among the Paliyan people during the 1990s. The first time he visited the Paliyan was in 1991 and after that he returned almost every year until 2003 when the dissertation was published. The study explores how a traditionally hunter-gatherer society sought to maintain autonomy while becoming increasingly integrated into regional labour markets and state structures. According to Norström social organization is characterized by strong ideals of individual autonomy, flexibility, and egalitarianism. His dissertation examines how these values shape the group's relations with neighbouring communities, non-governmental organizations, and indigenous-rights movements. There is a collection of photographs at the Museum of Ethnography, Stockholm Norström's 1991 fieldwork. Andaman Islands Norström has also conducted fieldwork in the Andaman Islands. Following his university studies, he received a scholarship that enabled him to travel to the islands, where he began field-based research on indigenous communities. During this period, he established contacts with the Society for Society for Andaman and Nicobar Ecology (SANE), a collaboration that has continued since. In an interview with the Swedish daily Dagens Nyheter in 2018, he talks about visiting the islands repeatedly between 1988 and 2014. In the interview he discussed the history and policies surrounding the indigenous peoples of the archipelago, including the Sentinelese. Fiction writing In addition to his academic publications, Norström has also written fiction. His crime novel Att dansa efter andras pipa was published in 2024. The novel is his first entry into crime fiction. References

title: Bandaragama
text: Bandaragama (Sinhala: බණ්ඩාරගම, Tamil: பண்டாரகம) is a suburb and town in the Kalutara District, Western Province, Sri Lanka. Located approximately 30 km (19 mi) south-east of Colombo, it serves as a residential, commercial, and transit hub linking the coastal belt with the interior towns of the Kalutara and Colombo districts. Administration and demographics Bandaragama serves as the administrative center for the Bandaragama Divisional Secretariat in the Kalutara District. According to the 2024 Sri Lankan Census, the Bandaragama Divisional Secretariat division recorded a population of 124,133 across a land area of 56.50 km2 (21.81 sq mi). Local municipal governance is overseen by the Bandaragama Pradeshiya Sabha. Geography Bandaragama is situated in the lowland wet zone of Sri Lanka. Its surrounding landscape consists of low-lying alluvial plains, wetlands, and agricultural land associated with the Bolgoda Lake system to the west and north-west. Economy Traditionally an agrarian area characterized by wet-rice paddy fields, rubber estates, and coconut cultivation, Bandaragama has developed into a commuter and commercial suburb due to its proximity to Colombo and major highway networks. Transport Bandaragama is a major road junction in the Western Province: Southern Expressway (E01): The Gelanigama Interchange connects Bandaragama directly to Sri Lanka's expressway network, providing high-speed access north toward Colombo and south toward Galle and Matara. A8 Highway (Panadura–Ratnapura Road): Runs directly through Bandaragama, linking the coastal town of Panadura in the west with Horana, Ingiriya, and Ratnapura in the east. Regional B-grade roads: Connected to neighboring towns via routes including the B254 (Kesbewa–Kindelpitiya–Bandaragama Road) and B458 (Waskaduwa–Bandaragama Road). Education Bandaragama falls under the Horana Educational Zone and the Bandaragama Educational Division. Notable schools in the division include Bandaragama Central College (Bandaragama Maha Vidyalaya), Pathahawatta Shri Swarnajothy Maha Vidyalaya, and Algassalie Muslim Primary School. Sports and recreation Bandaragama is home to the Sri Lanka Karting Circuit (SpeedBay Bandaragama), an FIA-CIK homologated international-standard karting track measuring approximately 1.2 km (0.75 mi) that hosts national motorsport and karting events.

title: Hu Xiaowei
text: Hu Xiaowei (Chinese: 胡小伟; born 1 May 1982), also known by the aliases Chen Xiaoer, Wu An Ming and Hu Shi, is a Chinese criminal, hacker and businessman who was affiliated with the Prince Group. He holds passports from China, Cambodia, Cyprus and Saint Kitts and Nevis, and a Hong Kong identity card. Born in Suqian, Jiangsu, China, Hu was involved in cases related to the "Knight Attack Group" network private server and illegal intrusion into computer systems in China in his early years. The Ministry of Public Security of China listed the case as a key case for supervision in 2010. When the case was closed in May 2011, reports indicated that other people involved in the case had been arrested, while Hu had fled the country, eventually moving to Cambodia in 2016. Subsequently, Zhang Gangyao, a former senior executive of the Prince Group, told the Organized Crime and Corruption Reporting Project that Hu had brought Chen Zhi, the main culprit in the Prince Group case, into the online gambling industry, and Chen Zhi called Hu "Big Brother"; the United States Department of the Treasury described Hu as the "second-in-command" of the Prince Group, while some Japanese media called him the "strategist". The U.S. sanctions document indicated that Hu established and supervised multiple related entities outside Cambodia, involving aviation, real estate and Hong Kong finance businesses. Since 2011, Hu has been engaged in business activities in Hong Kong under different aliases. In 2018, he took over a Hong Kong listed company as "Chen Xiaoer" and became its chairman; reports indicate that he subsequently purchased properties in Hong Kong and the United Kingdom and owned multiple aircraft through a Hong Kong company. In 2022, he was appointed as an advisor to Heng Samrin, the President of the National Assembly of Cambodia. The United States and the United Kingdom have listed Prince Group as a transnational criminal organization since October 2025 and imposed sanctions on related individuals and entities. Hu was already on the U.S. sanctions list under the alias "Chen Xiaoer" at that time, and the United Kingdom and the United States subsequently announced several of his aliases and related companies. The Hong Kong High Court has frozen the assets of Chen Zhi, Hu Xiaowei and Li Tian, totaling approximately HK$8.9 billion; Singapore Police Force have frozen hundreds of millions of assets during their investigation of the Prince Group case and stated that they had seized Hu's bank and securities accounts in Singapore. On 14 June 2026, Hu, who holds a "highly skilled professional" residence status in Japan, was arrested in Osaka for allegedly submitting a false immigration declaration. He was later arrested again for allegedly violating the Immigration Control and Refugee Recognition Act and was fined by the Japanese authorities through a summary procedure. According to Japanese media reports, he left Japan on 29 July 2026 and was extradited to the United States. Early life Hu Xiaowei was born in Suqian, Jiangsu in 1982. He studied at Suqian Middle School in Jiangsu in his early years and donated money to his alma mater in 2016. In 2005, after graduating from Chongqing University, he stayed in Chongqing and worked as the marketing manager of Internet data center business in a local electronics company. In early 2007, Cai Wen, the main culprit in the "Knight Group" private server and illegal computer intrusion case, rented a server from the company where Hu worked, and the two became acquainted. He then fled to Chongqing and recruited Hu to resume the advertising agency business of the private server of The Legend of Mir 2. title: Yücel Yılmaz
text: Yücel Yılmaz (born 10 July 1975) is a Turkish businessman and politician who served as the Mayor of Balıkesir from 2019 to 2024 and as the President of the Union of Municipalities of Turkey from 2023 to 2024. Early life and career Yılmaz was born on 10 July 1975 in Bottrop, West Germany, before moving to Balıkesir, Turkey, with his family at a young age. He graduated from Anadolu University Faculty of Education with a degree in English Language Teaching, and later completed a master's degree in International Economics and Trade Policy at İzmir Democracy University. After working as an English teacher in state schools, he received training in language school management in Canada and subsequently founded YDS Academy, a chain of foreign language schools operating across Turkey. Prior to entering politics, he served as the Assembly President of the Balıkesir Chamber of Commerce. Political career In the 2014 Turkish local elections, Yılmaz was elected Mayor of the newly established Karesi district of Balıkesir as a candidate of the Justice and Development Party (AKP). In the 2019 Turkish local elections, he was elected Mayor of Balıkesir, defeating İsmail Ok and taking office on 8 April 2019. On 31 May 2023, he was elected President of the Union of Municipalities of Turkey (TBB), succeeding Fatma Şahin. He ran for re-election as Mayor of Balıkesir in the 2024 Turkish local elections, but was defeated by Ahmet Akın and left office in April 2024. Personal life Yılmaz is married to Mehtap Yılmaz and has three children. References

title: Muharrem Erkek
text: Muharrem Erkek (born 31 August 1969) is a Turkish lawyer and politician serving as the Mayor of Çanakkale since April 2024. He previously served as a member of the Grand National Assembly of Turkey for Çanakkale from 2015 to 2023 and as the acting Secretary General of the Republican People's Party (CHP) from 2019 to 2020. Early life and education Erkek was born on 31 August 1969 in Çanakkale, Turkey. He graduated from Istanbul University Faculty of Law and began working as an independent lawyer registered with the Çanakkale Bar Association in 1994. Between 2000 and 2002, he served on the executive board of the Çanakkale Bar Association. Political career From 2004 to 2014, Erkek served as a member of the Çanakkale Municipal Council and held the position of deputy mayor. During this period, he also served on the board of directors of Çanakkale Dardanelspor and the Çanakkale City Council Executive Board. He was elected to the Grand National Assembly of Turkey representing Çanakkale in the June 2015 Turkish general election, and was subsequently re-elected in the November 2015 and 2018 general elections, serving through the 25th, 26th, and 27th parliamentary terms. On 12 February 2018, he was appointed Deputy Chairman of the Republican People's Party responsible for legal policies. Following the resignation of Mehmet Akif Hamzaçebi on 11 February 2019, Erkek assumed the role of acting Secretary General of the CHP until 10 August 2020. He resigned from the party's Central Executive Board (MYK) on 1 June 2023. In the 2024 Turkish local elections, Erkek ran as the CHP candidate for Mayor of Çanakkale and won the election, taking office on 9 April 2024. Personal life Erkek is married and has two children. title: Marie Chiha Hadad
text: Marie Chiha Hadad (also Marie Hadad; 12 March 1889 – 1 January 1973), was a Lebanese painter and writer. She began painting in the 1920s and established a professional career during the following decade. Portraits of Bedouins, villagers and other rural subjects figured heavily in her work. During the 1930s, she exhibited in Beirut and Paris and participated in the Salon d'Automne. She was also among the Lebanese artists whose work was shown at the 1939 New York World's Fair. Early life Marie Chiha was born on 12 March 1889 in Bmekkine, in the Mount Lebanon Mutasarrifate of the Ottoman Empire. Her father, Antoine Chiha, was a Chaldean Catholic of Iraqi origin who became a banker in Beirut in partnership with members of the Pharaon family, to which Hadad's mother belonged. Hadad grew up in Beirut and attended the French-language Catholic Collège Notre-Dame des Sœurs de Nazareth, graduating in 1908. In 1916, she married Georges Hadad, and subsequently used his surname professionally. They had three daughters. Her brother was the banker and political thinker Michel Chiha. Her sister was married to Bechara El Khoury, who later became president of Lebanon. Career Hadad began painting independently in the mid-1920s. She later received private lessons from the Polish painter Jan Kober, who worked in the Levant and taught women belonging to Beirut's upper social circles. Unlike the contemporary Lebanese painters Moustafa Farroukh, Omar Onsi and César Gemayel, who received artistic training abroad, Hadad did not attend art school. By the 1930s, Hadad was exhibiting professionally in Beirut. Her husband helped arrange exhibitions. In December 1933, she held an exhibition in the ballroom of the Saint Georges Hotel in Beirut, under the patronage of French High Commissioner Damien de Martel. Hadad concentrated particularly on portraits of peasants and Bedouins. This differed from the landscape painting that predominated in the work of male contemporary artists Farroukh, Onsi and Gemayel. The Lebanese art historian and curator Marie Tomb compares Hadad's work to Fauvism, particularly her use of flat areas of saturated color and thick outlines. Her subjects also included people from the Lebanese mountains. In addition to these portraits, she painted landscapes, still lifes, relatives and friends, and female nudes. Bedouin subjects became so associated with her work that the Venice Biennale later referred to her by the sobriquet "the Bedouin's artist". Hadad developed a career in Paris during the 1930s alongside her exhibitions in Beirut. Tomb describes her as having achieved greater recognition there than the other leading Lebanese painters of her generation. Her solo exhibitions included shows at Galerie Bernheim in 1933, Galerie Rotgé in 1937 and Galerie Borghese in 1939. The French art critic Louis Vauxcelles supported Hadad's work and wrote texts for exhibition catalogues accompanying shows in Beirut and Paris. Vauxcelles had earlier coined the term Fauves in his criticism of the artists associated with Henri Matisse. Hadad exhibited at the Salon d'Automne at the Grand Palais in 1933, 1934, 1935 and 1937. In 1934, the Jeu de Paume Museum acquired one of her paintings. In Beirut, she continued exhibiting in the late 1930s and early 1940s. She participated in exhibitions organised by the Association des Amis des Arts, including its salons of 1938, 1939 and 1940. Hadad was one of the artists selected for the Lebanese Republic pavilion at the 1939 New York World's Fair. The pavilion was organised by the writer and businessman Charles Corm. Hadad's contribution was a painting of two Lebanese women making bread. The latter painting, titled Two Women Kneading Dough, dates from around 1938 and is held by the Dahesh Museum of Art. Hadad also wrote in French. In 1937, she published Les Heures libanaises, a collection of short stories illustrated with reproductions of her paintings. title: Hugh Smith (footballer)
text: Hugh Smith (born 11 November 2006) is an Irish professional footballer who plays as a forward for League of Ireland Premier Division club UCD. Club career Early life & career Smith joined Shelbourne's academy in 2019, initially at under-13 level, remaining there until 2022 when he joined the academy at Dundalk in 2022, spending 2 years there before joining Bohemians' academy in 2024. He attended school at Belvedere College and was part of the team that were runners up in the FAI Schools Cup in April 2024. Bohemians On 22 January 2024, Smith made his debut for a young Bohemians side in a 3–1 defeat away to Drogheda United in the Leinster Senior Cup, scoring his side's goal. On 3 February 2025, he scored in a 6–3 win over Wexford in the Leinster Senior Cup. On 23 May 2025, he made his senior league debut, replacing James Clarke in the 83rd minute of a 1–0 loss away to Drogheda United, on what proved to be his final appearance for the club. UCD In July 2025, he signed for League of Ireland First Division club UCD. He made his debut for the club on 18 July 2025 in a 3–0 defeat to Finn Harps in an FAI Cup tie at Finn Park. He scored 4 goals in 15 games by the end of the 2025 season. On 16 October 2026, he scored the first Hat-trick of his senior career, in a 5–2 win away to Wexford at Ferrycarrig Park in the final league game of the regular season. He continued his form into the 2026 League of Ireland play-offs, scoring in both legs against Longford Town, scored in the following round in a 3–1 win over Bray Wanderers and assisted the winner in the promotion/relegation final as UCD defeated Drogheda United 2–1 at Tallaght Stadium to earn promotion to the League of Ireland Premier Division. He scored an impressive 19 goals in 42 appearances across all competitions in 2026. Personal life After enrolling at University College Dublin in 2025, Smith began a degree in Economics and Finance. title: Insomnia (Riize song)
text: "Insomnia" is a song recorded by South Korean boy band Riize. It was released on October 25, 2026, through SM Entertainment and distributed by Kakao Entertainment and RCA Records. Background and release In August 2026, SM Entertainment released their annual earnings report for the second quarter 0f 2026. In that report, Riize was mentioned to release a new music in fourth quarter of 2026. On October 19, 2026, it was announced that Riize would release a digital single titled "Insomnia". On October 21, a short preview for the song and promotional release schedule were released. Four days later, the music video teaser was released alongside with teaser photos. The song and the music video were released on October 25. Minjae Kim directed the music video. Composition Lyrics for "Insomnia" were written by Kim Eana. Jonathan Yip, Ray Romulus, Jeremy Reeves, August Rigo, and Kosmic made additional contributions to composition, with The Stereotypes produce the song. "Insomnia" is an acoustic pop song characterized by its guitar-based instrumentation and subdued atmosphere. The lyrics describe thoughts toward another person that grow clearer late at night, as well as the complex emotions that emerge from those feelings. Promotion Riize performed the song on various music shows, KBS's Music Bank on October 30 and November 6, MBC's Show! Music Core on October 31 and November 7, and SBS's Inkigayo on November 1 and November 8, They also performed the song on 2026 Melon Music Awards on November 14.
