title: Amado Picardal
text: Fr. Amado Picardal, CSsR (October 6, 1954 – May 29, 2024), often referred to as the "cycling priest" and also known by his nickname as "Father Picx", was a human rights and peace advocate, poet, endurance cyclist, theology professor, and Filipino Redemptorist Catholic priest best known for his decades of opposition to authoritarian abuses and to extra-judicial killings, most prominently during the time of Martial law under Ferdinand Marcos and of the Philippine Drug War under Rodrigo Duterte. Picardal became a student activist while studying Philosophy at the University of San Carlos in Cebu from 1971 to 1975, which coincided with Ferdinand Marcos' August 1971 suspension of the Writ of Habeas Corpus and his eventual September 1972 Proclamation of Martial Law. As a result, Picardal was arrested, tortured, and became a political detainee at Camp Sergio Osmeña, the Lahug Detention Center and Camp Lapulapu Detention and Rehabilitation Center for a total of seven months, from September 21, 1973 to April 15, 1974. After college, he professed vows as a Redemptorist in 1977 and was ordained in 1981, having finished his theological studies at the St. Francis Regional Major Seminary in Davao City. Picardal spent much of the 1980s helping to build build Basic Ecclesial Communities (BECs) througout Mindanao, and helped mobilize communities against commercial logging in Bukidnon until a provincial logging ban was finally established in 1989. In 1999, he co-founded the Coalition Against Summary Executions, which helped document more than a thousand extrajudicial killings associated with the Davao Death Squad. When Davao Mayor Rodrigo Duterte was elected president in 2016 and launched the Philippine Drug War, Picardal became one of its loudest critics. Picardal was also well known as an endurance cyclist, using his trips as a venue for advocacy and awareness building. He cycled 2,083 km from Davao to Ilocos Norte 2000 as part of his peace advocacy, and later cycled more than 5,000 km during round-trip route from Davao to Aparri and back in 56 days in 2008. Picardal died of a heart attack on May 29, 2024.

title: On Žižka's Battle Waggon
text: On Žižka's War Wagon (Czech: Na Žižkově válečném voze) is a 1968 Czechoslovak historical adventure film directed by Milan Vošmik. Set during the Hussite Wars, the film follows two boys, Ondra and Sulík, who become involved in the conflict and attempt to rescue Ondra's captured father. The film stars Josef Filip, Jan Kraus and Ilja Prachař. It was the final completed film directed by Vošmik. The film was also known as Ondra´s fight for freedom. Plot The widowed yeoman Tůma and his household set out to assist the town of Kouřim, which has come under attack by Catholic forces. His son Ondra secretly follows him, forcing the castellan Mikšík, who is responsible for the boy, to pursue him. Both are captured by soldiers from Kutná Hora, but Mikšík sacrifices himself to help Ondra escape. During his journey, Ondra meets Sulík, an orphan, and the two boys become friends. Upon returning home, they discover that Tůma's fortress has been burned down. They decide to seek out the camp of the Hussite commander Jan Žižka. While resting in an abandoned mill, the boys overhear enemy soldiers discussing an ambush planned against Žižka's forces. They steal the soldiers' horses and ride to warn the Hussites, helping them defeat the forces of Hynek Krušina of Švamberk. Ondra subsequently learns that his father is being held captive by Švamberk. He attempts to rescue him on his own but is captured and sentenced to be burned at the stake. Sulík and the Hussite warrior Vít Pračka manage to save him. Žižka then proposes exchanging three captured knights for Tůma. During the exchange, Švamberk's men betray the agreement and attack the Hussite delegation. Ondra, Sulík, Pračka and Tůma fight back and overcome their opponents. In the end, Ondra is reunited with his father, while Sulík finds a new protector in Pračka. Cast Josef Filip as Ondra of Koleč Jan Kraus as Sulík František Hanus as Vít Pračka Vladimír Ráž as Tůma of Koleč Ilja Prachař as Jan Žižka Martin Růžek as Hynek Krušina of Švamberk František Filipovský as Adam Chrůst František Smolík as Sivá hlava Josef Větrovec as Mikšík Vladimír Hrubý as Konrad Hornung Karel Smyczek as Kuno Production The film was directed by Milan Vošmik and based on a book by Josef František Karas of the same name. The screenplay was written by J. A. Novotný. Cinematography was handled by Jan Novák, while the music was composed by Svatopluk Havelka. The film was produced by Barrandov Studios. Filming began on 7 February 1968 and concluded on 12 June of the same year. The first completed print was approved on 15 August 1968. The film was Vošmik's final completed directorial work. The cast included several established Czechoslovak actors, including Ilja Prachař as Jan Žižka and Martin Růžek as Hynek Krušina of Švamberk. Release The film premiered in Czechoslovakia on 29 November 1968. It was classified as suitable for young audiences. The film had a running time of 73 minutes.

title: King of Time (Johnny Clegg album)
text: King of Time is the fifth and final studio album by South African singer Johnny Clegg. Released on 27 October 2017 during Clegg's Final Journey tour, after his cancer diagnosis in 2015 and was his first album since 2010's Human. The album was recorded at B# studios in Johannesburg and was produced by Denholm Harding and John Paul De Stefani and features collaborations with Clegg's son Jesse and French- Beninese singer Angélique Kidjo. Background Clegg had been diagnosed with pancreatic cancer in 2015 but by 2017 he had gone into remission and set out on his Final Journey World tour which included shows across Europe, US and South Africa. Clegg's son, Jesse also joined him on the tour and would contribute to the album, writing and dueting the song I've Been Looking with his father. In a music video uploaded to youtube, the song was dedicated to Johnny by his son, just as he had dedicated the song Cruel, Crazy, Beautiful World on the Savuka album of the same name to Jesse. The title track "King of Time" was released as the lead single for the album mentions aspects of Cleggs musical influence from both western and Zulu culture with the lyrics "My crazy ballerina loves the Zulu concertina." Colour of My Skin, with backing vocals with singer Angélique Kidjo reflects on Cleggs experience as an Anthropologist. The song Oceanearth also tackles issues relating to enviromentalism, with lyrics referring to the destruction of coral reefs. Reception The album was received well by fans as it was seen as Cleggs farwell album and would be his last after his death in July 2019. The Facebook fan page "Scatterlings of Africa" ranked the album the 8th best out of Cleggs entire discography, including his works with Juluka and Savuka. In an interview Clegg described the album as a "celebration of 40 years of music." He also said the album was part of "a three year idea...that I would do a Final Journey Tour, an album and do an Autobiography." The mentioned autobiography titled "Scatterling of Africa" would be released posthumously in 2021 and would cover Cleggs early childhood and adult life. Track Listing *There was also a 10 track release including bonus live tracks such as Woza Friday, Impi and Dela

title: Tilak Agerwala
text: Tilak Agerwala is a computer engineer. His work with John Cocke contributed to the development of IBM's RS/6000 systems and the architecture associated with superscalar processing. He spent 35 years at IBM conducting research and executive positions and worked on processor architecture, parallel systems and supercomputing. He received the W. Wallace McDowell Award in 1998 and is a Fellow of the Institute of Electrical and Electronics Engineers (IEEE). Education Agerwala received a Bachelor of Technology degree in electrical engineering from the Indian Institute of Technology Kanpur in 1971. He subsequently attended Johns Hopkins University, where he earned a PhD in electrical engineering in 1975. His doctoral dissertation was titled Towards a Theory for the Analysis and Synthesis of Systems Exhibiting Concurrency. Career Agerwala joined the faculty of the University of Texas at Austin, where he was an assistant professor of electrical engineering from 1975 to 1978. In 1979, he joined IBM's Thomas J. Watson Research Center. He collaborated with computer architect John Cocke on the development of a processor architecture that became the basis for IBM's RS/6000 workstation line. From 1989 to 1992, Agerwala served as director of future systems technologies at IBM. He directed the systems architecture and technology strategy for the IBM RS/6000 SP from 1992 to 1997. The system used interconnected RS/6000 processors and was designed for scalable parallel computing. From 1997 to 1998, he served as director of server architecture and systems strategy in IBM's server development organization. From 2013 to 2014, he served as vice president of Data-Centric Systems at IBM Research. His group worked on architectures for scalable, data-intensive computing. The initiative was associated with the development of systems for large-scale scientific and commercial workloads, including IBM's work on the Summit supercomputer for Oak Ridge National Laboratory. He has served as an adjunct associate professor at Pace University and an adjunct professor at the National Institute of Advanced Studies in Bangalore. In 2019, he held the Dr. S. Radhakrishnan Visiting Chair at the institute. Research Agerwala's research has addressed computer architecture, concurrency, processor design and parallel algorithms. His early publications examined the analysis of concurrent systems, Petri nets, data-flow computing and methods for modelling processor performance. In a 1979 paper with K. Mani Chandy and D. E. Lang, he presented a modelling approach and design tool for analysing pipelined central processors. In the 1980s, his work with John Cocke addressed processor designs capable of executing multiple instructions in parallel. The term superscalar was introduced in connection with ideas described by the two researchers in talks during the decade. Their work helped establish the architectural approach used in IBM's POWER1 processor and RS/6000 systems. According to computer architects John L. Hennessy and David A. Patterson, Agerwala and John Cocke described key ideas related to instruction-level parallelism in talks during the mid-1980s and coined the term ‘superscalar.’ They associated these ideas with the development of IBM's POWER1 architecture. Agerwala also worked on the architecture of scalable parallel computers. His contributions to the IBM SP2 were described in research papers examining its distributed-memory architecture, processor interconnection network and system software. The SP2 used RS/6000 processors connected through a multistage, packet-switched network and supported applications requiring large-scale parallel computation. Awards and honors IEEE Fellow, for contributions to high-performance computer development. 1998 W. Wallace McDowell Award, presented by the IEEE Computer Society for contributions to the development of high-performance computers. Founding member of the IBM Academy of Technology. 2019 Dr. S. Radhakrishnan Visiting Chair Professo

title: Statue of Gaspar Corte-Real
text: A statue of Portuguese explorer Gaspar Corte-Real stands on the grounds of the Confederation Building in St. John's, Newfoundland and Labrador, Canada. It was designed by Portuguese sculptor Martins Correira and erected in 1965 as a gift from the government of Portugal to the government of Newfoundland. In the 2020s, the statue has come under criticism both for Corte-Real's actions during his explorations—which included the abduction of several dozen indigenous people—as well as for its connections to Portuguese dictator António de Oliveira Salazar. Design The monument is located on the grounds in front of the Confederation Building, across the street from the building on the other side of the Parkway. It consists of a bronze statue of Gaspar Corte-Real, made of bronze, which stands 24 feet (7.3 metres) tall and weighs approximately 3.5 short tons. The statue faces towards the harbour of St. John's. An inscription attached to the monument reads as follows: Gaspar Corte-Real, Portuguese navigator—he reached Terra Nova in the 15th century—at the beginning of the era of the great discoveries. From the Portuguese Fisheries Organization—an expression of gratitude on behalf of the Portuguese Grand Banks fishermen for the friendly hospitality always extended to them by the people of Terra Nova, May 1965. History Background on Corte-Real Gaspar Corte-Real was a Portuguese explorer who, in 1500 and 1501, made two expeditions to the Americas. While the exact location charted by Corte-Real is unknown, based on descriptions, several historians believe it was the coasts of modern-day Labrador and Newfoundland. Some historians, such as William Gilbert Gosling, have speculated that Corte-Real named several locations in the province, including Conception Bay and Portugal Cove. During the 1501 expedition, Corte-Real's crew captured about sixty indigenous people. However, Corte-Real's ship disappeared during this voyage. Creation of the statue In 1963, a Portuguese ambassador in Canada suggested the creation of a statue of Corte-Real to celebrate the cultural ties between Portugal and Newfoundland. The idea was supported by Newfoundland Premier Joey Smallwood, who said that he would have the statue placed in front of the Confederation Building on Portuguese soil and would additionally proclaim an annual "Portugal Day" holiday in the province. In 1965, the statue was erected, having been donated by the government of Portugal to the government of Newfoundland in recognition of the positive relationship and shared history between the two polities. Specifically, the statue was given on behalf of the Portuguese Fisheries Organization in recognition of the hospitality offered by the people of Newfoundland, especially along the Grand Banks of Newfoundland. The statue had been designed by Portuguese sculptor Martins Correira and made in the artist's studio in Lisbon. The statue was erected on the grounds of the Confederation Building as part of a project by Smallwood to have several monuments and memorials commemorating the province's history placed around the building. As part of the plan, Smallwood intended to request the governments of several countries to send statues of figures who had a shared history to both the donating country and Newfoundland. For example, he had planned to request that the federal government of the United States send a statue of Squanto, a Native American who had lived in the territory of both modern-day Newfoundland and the United States. However, the Corte-Real statue is the only one that the Newfoundland government received from a foreign government. In a 1989 book discussing this plan, Newfoundland author and politician Harold Horwood noted that António de Oliveira Salazar, the dictator of Portugal at the time that the statue had been donated, had been a friend of Smallwood's. For the statue's dedication ceremony, Smallwood had invited Salazar. In addition to the Corte-Real statue, Smallwood commissioned sculptor Hans Me

title: Agam Buhbut
text: Agam Buhbut (Hebrew: אגם בוחבוט) is an Israeli pop singer. She first became known as a child contestant on the second season of the television music show Beit Sefer LeMusika (School of Music), and was mentored for about a decade by singer Moshe Peretz. She released her debut album at 18 in 2022, the year she topped Israel's YouTube music chart, and three of her songs, including "Kulam Ganavim", appeared in the top ten of Ice's ranking of Israel's songs of the Hebrew year 5786 (2025–26). Career Early career Buhbut came to public attention about 2013 on Beit Sefer LeMusika, a music competition for children. That year she recorded the duet "Yalda Ktana" ("Little Girl") with Moshe Peretz, who also wrote her song "Kvar Lo Yalda Ktana" ("No Longer a Little Girl"). Her breakthrough hit was "Yahalom" ("Diamond"), followed by "Kol HaOlam" and "Magavot" ("Towels"), her first collaboration with producer Jordi. She also released "Bati Lehatzil Otach" with Shachar Saul and appeared on Saul and Noroz's "Dovshaniya". Debut album and chart success (2022–2024) In February 2022, at the age of 18, Buhbut released her debut album, whose cover displayed only her first name. Its songs included "Shahor Teltan", "Shirei Dika'on" and "Ata Lo Bareshimot". Reviewing it for Mako, Dor Meir Muallem compared her music to the pop of Dua Lipa and Eden Ben Zaken and wrote that she was on her way to becoming Israel's biggest pop star. At the end of 2022, she was at the top of YouTube's annual music chart in Israel, succeeding Eden Ben Zaken, who had held the spot the previous year. In 2023, at the age of 19, Buhbut ended her professional relationship with Peretz. She later released "Nadi Badi", a duet with Shachar Tabuch. Later career (2025–present) In 2025, Buhbut released her first songs written by herself, including a song about her partner. Her later releases include the album Esrim Ve'Ahat (Twenty-One) and the mini-album Life Lately. In Ice's year-end ranking for 5786 (2025–26), "Kulam Ganavim" ("Everyone's a Thief"), from Life Lately, placed second, with about 23 million YouTube views and over 14 million Spotify streams; "Eich She'hi Rokedet" ("The Way She Dances"), with Eden Hason and Ofek Adanek, placed sixth; and "HaMabat Be'einech" ("The Look in Your Eyes"), from Esrim Ve'Ahat, placed eighth. In June 2026, she released "Sipur Chayai" ("The Story of My Life"), her first collaboration with producer and songwriter Mistermiss, who wrote it for her; it was released during Pride Month as a song about self-acceptance. At a concert in Caesarea that month, she performed a song she had co-written with Yonatan Klimi and Tamar Yehalomi for her brother's wedding. Acting Buhbut appeared in the youth series Kfula. She has also played an intelligence officer in a series on Keshet 12, though she has said that her focus is music. Personal life Buhbut has been in a relationship with actor Bar Brimer since about 2021; they met on the set of Kfula, where he appeared in one of her music videos. In September 2026, the couple announced their engagement. Discography Albums Debut album (2022) Esrim Ve'Ahat (Twenty-One) Life Lately (mini-album) Selected singles "Yalda Ktana" (with Moshe Peretz, 2013) "Yahalom" "Kol HaOlam" "Magavot" "Nadi Badi" (with Shachar Tabuch) "Kulam Ganavim" "Eich She'hi Rokedet" (with Eden Hason and Ofek Adanek) "HaMabat Be'einech" "Sipur Chayai" (2026) References

title: Team Hurricane
text: Team Hurricane is a 2017 Danish docudrama film written and directed by Annika Berg, at her feature film debut. It premiered at the 74th edition of the Venice Film Festival, in the International Critics' Week sidebar. Plot Cast Eja Penelope Roepstorff as Eja Ida Glitre as Ida Ira Rønnenfelt as Ira Maja Leth Bang as Maja Mathilde Linnea Daugaard Jensen as Mathilde Mia My Elise Pedersen as Mia Sara Morling as Sara Zara Munch Bjarnum as Zara Søren Pedersen as Søren Production The film had the working title Forever 13. It was produced by Adomeit Film. It had a budget of €400,000. Its cast consists of non-professional actors, that director Annika Berg chose after an intense search on social networks. Berg initially planned to focus on four protagonists, but expanded the story to eight characters following a workshop with ten candidates. The script consisted of rough outlines of scenes, not of pre-written lines, and the dialogue was improvised on the spot, during the girls' interactions. Release The film had its world premiere at the 74th Venice International Film Festival, in the International Critics' Week section. It premiered in Danish cinemas on 11 September 2026. Reception The film was well-received by critics. Cineuropa critic Kaleem Aftab described it as "an exciting, radical punk film", with "eclectic and colourful characters" and "a unique aesthetic and tone: it mixes the realism of handheld cameras and documentary footage with the colour palette of a Japanese anime". Sean Gallen from The Upcoming called it "a poignant and inclusive exploration of burgeoning femininity" in which Berg "achieves authenticity by providing substance behind the style". Berlingske critic Jacob Wendt Jensen referred to it as "a hurricane of a film" which was "experimental on several levels". At the Venice Film Festival, it won the Verona Film Club Award, an award given to the most innovative in the Critics' Week sidebar. It was nominated to two Bodil Awards, for Best Film and Best Actress, with the latter nomination going to the ensemble cast as a whole. It also received four Robert Awards nominations, including for Best Director.

title: Jorge Martinez-Vazquez
text: Jorge Martínez-Vázquez is a Spanish-American economist and the Regents Professor Emeritus of Economics at Georgia State University. He is the founding director of its International Center for Public Policy. Education Martínez-Vázquez studied economics and law at the University of Barcelona, graduating in economics in 1970 and law in 1971. He also studied political science at the Complutense University of Madrid. In 1973, he received a Fulbright-Hays scholarship to pursue graduate studies in the United States. He earned a Master of Arts in economics from Washington University in St. Louis in 1974 and a PhD in economics from the same university in 1979. Academic career Martínez-Vázquez joined the Department of Economics at Georgia State University in 1977 as an assistant professor. He became an associate professor in 1983 and a professor in 1989. In 2008, the University System of Georgia appointed him a Regents Professor. He became Regents Professor Emeritus in 2021. In 1996, he established the International Studies Program at Georgia State University's Andrew Young School of Policy Studies. He has also held visiting academic appointments at institutions in Spain, including the Universidad Carlos III de Madrid and the Instituto de Estudios Fiscales. International policy work Martínez-Vázquez has been a member of the IMF's Panel of Fiscal Experts since 1994. From 1997 to 2000, he directed the Georgia State University–USAID Fiscal Reform Project in the Russian Federation. He also directed a World Bank tax policy review project in Pakistan in 2007–2008, and worked on fiscal decentralization and tax administration projects in countries including Indonesia, Cambodia, Egypt, Peru, Tanzania and North Macedonia. Research In a 2003 article co-authored with Robert McNab and published in World Development, Martínez-Vázquez examined the relationship between fiscal decentralization and economic growth. His collaborative research with economists including James Alm, Richard Bird, Sally Wallace and Benno Torgler has examined the institutional and behavioural factors affecting tax compliance. His work on taxation has also considered the relationship between government institutions, public trust and taxpayers' willingness to comply with tax obligations, particularly in developing and transition economies. His research on public finance has examined government budgeting, public expenditure, fiscal management and the financing of local services. He has also contributed to comparative studies of fiscal systems in developing and transition economies, including research on the relationship between decentralization, institutional quality and economic development. Awards and recognition In 1997, Martínez-Vázquez became a member of the Russian Academy of Natural Sciences. In 2006, he was appointed an honorary professor of the China Public Finance and Public Policy Academy at the Central University of Finance and Economics in Beijing. The University of Vigo awarded him an honorary doctorate in 2011. In 2010, he received the Russian Federation National Prize in Economics for the 2007–2009 period, jointly with Yuriy Gorodnichenko and Klara Sabirianova Peter. In the same year, he received the Public Policy Award of the International Institute of Public Finance, presented in connection with German development cooperation. In 2018, he was a Distinguished Academic Visitor at the Lee Kuan Yew School of Public Policy. In 2020, Georgia State University presented him with its Sheth Distinguished Faculty Award for International Achievement. In 2022, he received the Elinor Ostrom Award for the best article published in the Journal of Theoretical Politics, jointly with co-authors. In 2023, he was elected a corresponding member of the Royal Galician Academy of Sciences. In July 2025, the University of Málaga awarded him an honorary doctorate in recognition of his work in economics, fiscal decentralization and public finance. References

title: Samy Komsan
text: Samy Komsan (Arabic: سامي قمصان; born 6 March 1976) is an Egyptian football coach and former player who played as a midfielder. He is the head coach of Al Mokawloon Al Arab. He spent most of his career at Al Ahly, first as a player in the late 1990s and later as assistant coach from 2018 to 2025. Playing career Komsan began his career with Al Ahly in 1997–98 and stayed until 2000–01, making 13 appearances, scoring once and winning the Egyptian Premier League twice. He then moved to Baladeyet El Mahalla in 2001, where he played one match, and joined Ismaily in 2002, making four appearances. He ended his playing career with Suez Cement in 2007–08. Managerial career Early career After retiring, Komsan worked as an assistant coach at Haras El Hodoud and El Sharkia. Al Ahly Komsan joined Al Ahly's technical staff in 2018 as an assistant coach and worked under Mohamed Youssef, Patrice Carteron, Martín Lasarte, René Weiler, Pitso Mosimane, Ricardo Soares and Marcel Koller. After Mosimane's departure in 2022 he was placed in temporary charge of the first team, leading it in six matches: four wins, one draw (against Zamalek) and one defeat (against Smouha). Following Koller's dismissal in April 2025, Qamsan, then general coach, resigned from his post. Al Mokawloon Al Arab On 5 October 2025, Al Mokawloon Al Arab appointed Komsan as head coach, replacing Mohamed Mekki. It was his first managerial role in the Egyptian Premier League. Personal life Komsan was born on 6 March 1976. Honours Player Al Ahly Egyptian Premier League: two titles during 1997–2001

title: Gerald Shaw
text: Gerald Shaw (1934 – 2 June 2026) was a South African political journalist best known for his coverage of South African politics in the last decades of the apartheid government. Most notably through the Political Survey column he wrote for the Cape Times newspaper from 1966 to 1996. Shaw grew up in Pretoria where he was educated by the Congregation of Christian Brothers and studied journalism at the University of Pretoria. He got his first job as a journalist at the Pretoria News newspaper. In 1957 he moved to the United Kingdom and worked at the Kentish Times, afterwhich he started working at the London office of the Cape Argus before moving back to South Africa to work at the Cape Times. Shaw's anti-apartheid feelings along with his critical coverage of the government made him unpopular with ruling National Party politicians. Whilst working as a political journalist in parliament he witnessed the assassination of the South African President after the man who delivered Shaw's lunch, Dimitri Tsafendas, stabbed President Hendrick Verwoerd a few moments after the delivery. He published a number of books about the history of the Cape Times newspaper and his own career as a journalist. His most notable book was his 2007 autobiography Believe in Miracles (ISBN 1919760709). He died at his home in Rondebosch, Cape Town in June 2026. References

title: Project Thadam
text: Project Thadam is a wildlife conservation and human–wildlife conflict mitigation initiative operated by the Tamil Nadu Forest Department in Tamil Nadu, India. The programme focuses on monitoring wild elephant movements, profiling individual elephants across forest divisions, and protecting the 42 identified elephant corridors in the state to reduce human fatalities and crop damage. History Project Thadam was launched in two primary phases. It was initially introduced on 1 September 2020 in the Coimbatore forest division as a localized communication network utilizing WhatsApp groups to share real-time alerts regarding elephant movements near human habitations. In April 2024, the initiative was expanded statewide under the Tamil Nadu Biodiversity Conservation and Greening Project for Climate Change Response, accompanied by a dedicated public web portal. Operations Under the initiative, forest officials identify and catalogue individual wild elephants based on distinctive physical characteristics, assigning unique identification numbers to track their migration patterns across divisions. Field personnel receive specialized training in elephant profiling and documentation at the Institute of Forest Genetics and Tree Breeding (IFGTB) in Coimbatore. To prevent elephants from straying into agricultural lands and settlements, the department maintains physical barriers such as elephant-proof trenches, solar-powered fences, hanging solar fences, and steel wire fences, while also constructing artificial waterholes and check dams inside forest boundaries. Early warning alerts are disseminated to local residents via SMS and messaging groups, and members of the public can report elephant sightings directly to forest authorities through the official Thadam portal.

title: Rosecraddock
text: Rosecraddock is a heritage-listed villa located in Caulfield North, in the City of Glen Eira, in the inner eastern suburbs of Melbourne, in Victoria, Australia. The house is situated at 2–8 Keverell Road and 4–10 Craddock Avenue. Built from 1857 on the traditional lands of the Bunurong people, the villa was added to the Victorian Heritage Register on 31 October 1984 in recognition of its historical and architectural significance; and was also added to non-statutory lists by the Victorian branch of the National Trust on 2 February 1984 and the now defunct Register of the National Estate on an unknown date. History Rosecraddock was constructed in two main stages. The first part was rated in 1857 as the home of Mr G. W. Harris. It consisted at that stage of seven rooms, a detached kitchen, servants' rooms, stable and outbuildings. Three successive owners over the next few years enlarged the building. No architect or builder's names are known for this work. By the 1870s when Henry Joseph Langdon owned the property, the house had been enlarged to fourteen rooms. This last increment of three or four rooms and stables was supervised by the architect, Lloyd Tayler. Langdon founded a firm of merchants and importers in 1852. The business is carried on by the family today and and has strong links with the maritime and building industries. Rosecradock remained in the family's ownership until 1984. The stables were moved from their original position in 1947 and their condition, as of November 1989, was not known. In 1984, Peter Shellard, an eccentric businessman, purchased Rosecraddock for A$1.4 million with plans to subdivide the 8,857-square-metre (95,340 sq ft) estate. His plans were thwarted by the property's inclusion on the Victorian Heritage Register; and in tragic circumstances, Shellard was murdered by his girlfriend and two accomplices at Rosecraddock in 2005. During Shellard's ownership of Rosecraddock, the estate fell into disrepair, and his estate sold the property in 2007 to Simone Semmens for A$7.8 million. Semmens subdivided the estate, and yielded $17.4 million by selling off the subdivided land, and $11 million for the restored villa, when it was purchased by Guy Russo, the chief executive of Kmart Australia. Description The villa is a twelve-room brick house with slate roof and stables set in extensive grounds. The property is enclosed by white paling fences and gates. The appearance of the building must have changed significantly because of the replacement of the existing verandah with one fashionable for the time and typical of Tayler's work. It was at this stage that the billiard room was added. The last extensions were in the 1880s boom years. The garden which was probably laid out about this time by a neighbour, Henry Ford, is now overgrown but intact. The property remains relatively unaltered from this time except for some redecoration of the interiors in the late twenties and the modification of the kitchen. The most interesting detail surviving from the nineteenth century is the intact decoration of the billiard room and dining room. The house is considered significant as an example of a substantial villa constructed and subsequently altered for well-to-do middle class families. Its continuous occupation by the Langdon family from the 1870s to the 1980s greatly assists in understanding the building and its garden surrounds as a document of upper middle-class Melbourne during the nineteenth and twentieth centuries.

title: Coral Europa
text: Coral Europa, branded since 2020 as just Coral, is a Portuguese television production company based in Lisbon. The company was established in 1988 as a division of Coral Visión, RCTV's distributor, into the European market, but later became autonomous from its Venezuelan parent, concentrating solely on the Portuguese market. History Coral Europa was established in Spain in 1988 under the presidency of Juan-Julio Baena. It initially had a six-year contract to supply Spanish television networks with telenovelas from its catalog, the first of which being Cristal, which aired on TVE1 in 1990. The company was tasked to distribute Coral International's catalog into Europe, Arabia and Africa. In 1993, the company signed its first Portuguese contact, with the airing of Topacio on TVI. Baena left the company in 1995 when his original contract ended, causing him to move to competing conglomerate Grupo Cisneros, distributing Venevisión telenovelas to Europe and Arabia under Visión Europa. The company still had agreements with TVE to air RCTV's telenovelas, but far from the success of the early 90s. As of September 1995, Coral Europa had a catalog of 11,000 hours worth of content, 70% of which were telenovelas. Coral Europa started producing content of its own in Portugal in 2007, with As Tardes da Júlia on TVI, when Júlia Pinheiro moved to SIC, it was also tasked to produce its successor program A Tarde é Sua in 2011. Beginning in 2009, it cooperated with Grupo V to launch an Iberian fishing and hunting channel, Cazavisión (Caçavision in Portugal), producing content for the channel. In 2012, it began producing Somos Portugal for TVI on Sunday afternoons. Despite its relations with TVI, Coral started producing content for other Portuguese networks. Still in 2012, it produced Dr. White for SIC and began producing its own fiction, beginning with Água de Mar on RTP1, and the drama biopic Jacinta in April 2017, timing with the centennary of the apparitions in Fátima. Beginning in January 2019, the company was responsible for producing morning shows with Cristina Ferreira, starting with O Programa da Cristina on SIC. She left the network to return to TVI in July 2020, where, from September of that year, was tasked to present Dia de Cristina, a series of occasional specials. She was planned to return to daily daytime presenting in 2021, but due to contractual reasons which also involved Coral Europa, she was unable to do so until 2023, and that Coral could not produce a competing program on TVI. On 1 June 2020, Coral Europa rebranded and began being branded as just Coral. In 2026, it was the largest debtor to Conta Lá, which shut down on 1 November, and demanded the channel's dissolution in court. References

title: Zhanna Gudkova
text: Zhanna Anatolyevna Gudkova (Russian: Жанна Анатольевна Гудкова; born December 27, 1987, Spassk-Dalny, Primorsky Krai, RSFSR, USSR) is a Russian politician who serves as a representative of the Legislative Assembly of Primorsky Krai in the Federation Council the upper house of the Russian parliament. She is a member of United Russia party. Biography Born on December 27, 1987, in the town of Spassk-Dalny, Primorsky Krai. In 2008, she graduated from the Primorsky Hydro-Melioration College, specializing in taxation. In 2012, she completed a degree in Finance and Credit at the Far Eastern Federal University. From 2013 to 2025, she worked for various commercial enterprises. Starting in 2025, she served as Deputy Director of the "Representation of the Government of Primorsky Krai to the Government of the Russian Federation" (a state-owned institution). She was a founder of the Varyag Charitable Foundation, named after her husband, Mikhail Gudkov, a two-time Hero of the Russian Federation. On September 20, 2026, she was elected as a deputy to the eighth convocation of the Legislative Assembly of Primorsky Krai via the unified electoral district. On September 30, she became the chair of the Committee on Budget and Tax Policy and Financial Resources. On October 21, 2026, she was appointed a senator of the Federation Council, effective as of October 5, 2026. She serves as a member of the Federation Council Committee on Regulations and Parliamentary Procedure. References

title: Mountain District Football Association
text: The Mountain District Football Association was an Australian rules football competition based in the Dandenong Ranges region of Victoria. History The Mountain District Football Association was first established in 1911 with Belgrave, Monbulk, Olinda and Ferny Creek competing. Monbulk dominated the competition's early years, with one source reporting that they had won 5 premierships in a row between 1912-1919 (ignoring years when football was in recess due to WWI). Emerald joined the competition for the first time in 1914. In 1921 the competition was re-named the Mountaineer Football Association, although this name would only last a year. The 1921 grand final between Monbulk and Ferntree Gully was drawn, with Monbulk winning the replay a week later. By 1924 the additions of Ferntree Gully, Gembrook, Macclesfield and Silvan had expanded the competition to 8 clubs, however the MDFA would enter recess only a year later when most clubs joined the newly-formed Scoresby District Football Association. The MDFA was re-established in 1930 by Emerald, Silvan, Gembrook, Ferny Creek and Monbulk. A year later the competition doubled in size when the SDFA folded and Belgrave, Boronia and Ferntree Gully all joined the MDFA, along with new clubs Mount Evelyn and Lilydale Imperials. The league slowly lost clubs over the next 4 years, with Ferntree Gully and Lilydale Imperials leaving in 1933, Boronia in 1934 and Mount Evelyn and Silvan in 1935. In 1936 Boronia re-joined along with Kilsyth and the MDFA was re-named the Belgrave District Football Association. This only lasted one season, however, and the competition disbanded in 1937, with clubs joining a number of surrounding leagues. The MDFA was not re-established until after WWII, when Belgrave, Emerald, Gembrook and Monbulk re-started football in the district. Olinda and Silvan both re-formed and joined a year later along with newly-formed clubs Upwey-Tecoma and South Belgrave. Cockatoo and Upper Ferntree Gully both formed and joined the MDFA in 1949, although the latter would depart after only 1 season and Cockatoo would only last 4 seasons before folding. Belgrave dominated the 1950s, winning 5 premierships in a row between 1950 and 1954. Further significant changes to the line-up of clubs in the final decade of the MDFA's existence came in 1957, when Ferntree Gully and Upper Ferntree Gully both re-joined the competition along with South Wantirna, and 1959 when Silvan departed for the Croydon-Ferntree Gully FL. The departures of Ferntree Gully, South Wantirna and Olinda to the Eastern Districts FL in 1965 signalled the end of the MDFA, and it would merge with the Yarra Valley FL in 1966 to form the Yarra Valley Mountain District Football League. title: Aleksey Orlov (politician, born 1967)
text: Aleksey Valeryevich Orlov (Russian: Алексей Валерьевич Орлов; born 20 March 1967) is a Russian politician who is serving a senator in the Federation Council since 15 October 2026, representing the legislative branch of Sverdlovsk Oblast. He is a member of the regional political council of the United Russia party as well as the First Deputy Secretary of the Sverdlovsk Regional Branch of the party. Biography He was born on March 20, 1967, in the settlement of Penya in the Tyumen Oblast. His mother was a trained librarian but worked in a canteen; his father was a driver and crane operator. He attended school first in Tobolsk, and later in the Kondinsky District of the Khanty-Mansi Autonomous Okrug. In 1992, he graduated from the Omsk Agricultural Institute (specializing in the "economics and organization of agricultural production"), and subsequently from the Tyumen Higher School of the Ministry of Internal Affairs of the Russian Federation (specializing in "jurisprudence"), qualifying as a legal professional. From 1993 to 2005, he served in the Russian Ministry of Internal Affairs, beginning his career as a district police officer. Until 1999, he worked in the Department for Combating Economic Crimes in Tobolsk, and later in the tax police, where he rose to the position of head of the operational division. In late 2005, he became a deputy to the head of Tobolsk, Yevgeny Kuyvashev. In July 2007, when Kuyvashev became the head of the Tyumen city administration, Orlov followed him, serving as his deputy for economics, finance, and taxation. In 2009, he worked as an advisor to the Governor of Tyumen Oblast, Vladimir Yakushev, and later headed the Office of the Federal Service for State Registration, Cadastre and Cartography for the Leningrad Oblast. Sverdlovsk Oblast government In July 2012, while serving as Governor of Sverdlovsk Oblast, Kuivashev appointed Orlov as Deputy Chairman of the regional government within the cabinet—new at the time—led by Denis Pasler. In this role, Orlov oversaw the development of the region's socio-economic strategy, financial, budgetary, and tax policy, the social sector, the implementation of priority national projects and demographic policy, and the balancing of labor resources. Orlov was also involved in organizing the Innoprom industrial trade fair. In September 2012, he became one of the deputy heads of the Sverdlovsk Oblast Investment Council[4]. On August 30, 2014, he was appointed First Deputy Chairman of the Sverdlovsk Oblast Government, concurrently serving as Minister of Investment and Development. In September 2016, following a government reorganization initiated by Kuivashev that saw the resignation of Pasler, Orlov effectively held the position of head of government for a period. In 2017, after the cabinet was placed under the direct authority of the governor, Orlov became the First Deputy Governor of Sverdlovsk Oblast. He oversaw the "Titanium Valley" special economic zone. Head of Yekaterinburg On December 21, 2020, he joined the Yekaterinburg City Administration, assuming the position of First Deputy to the Head of Yekaterinburg, Alexander Vysokinsky. The following day, he became the Acting Head of the city after Vysokinsky's resignation. On February 9, 2021, the Yekaterinburg City Duma confirmed Orlov as the Head of Yekaterinburg for a five-year term. Significant changes took place in Yekaterinburg's public transport sector. The city acquired hundreds of new buses, retired old, worn-out trolleybuses, and introduced modern trams. The public transport network and its routes were also reorganized. A controversial reform of street commerce was implemented, altering the layout and terms for the placement of kiosks. Kiosks across the city—including those at public transport stops—were demolished en masse, leaving passengers without shelter while waiting for transport. Nearly all newsstands were torn down. title: Martyn T. Smith
text: Martyn Thomas Smith is a Distinguished Emeritus Professor of toxicology in the School of Public Health at the University of California, Berkeley. He has directed the Superfund Research Program Center at the university since its establishment in 1987. Early life and education Smith received a PhD in biochemistry from St Bartholomew's Hospital in London and then completed postdoctoral training in toxicology at the Karolinska Institute in Stockholm. Career Smith became director of the University of California, Berkeley Superfund Research Program Center at its establishment in 1987. The National Institute of Environmental Health Sciences has funded the center continuously under grant P42ES004705 since 1987. In 1994, Lawrence Berkeley Laboratory listed Smith as one of its scientists in Energy and Environment. Smith served on the National Academies of Sciences, Engineering, and Medicine committee that produced the 2023 report Building Confidence in New Evidence Streams for Human Health Risk Assessment. In 2023, he became the president and chief executive officer of 1Tox, a consulting company. He is a distinguished emeritus professor of toxicology and holds the Kaiser Chair of Cancer Epidemiology in the Division of Environmental Health Sciences at UC Berkeley. Research In December 2004, Science published a study of benzene-exposed workers by Smith and colleagues from the United States and the Chinese Center for Disease Control and Prevention. The researchers tracked 250 workers at a shoe factory near Tianjin for 16 months and compared them with workers at a nearby clothing factory. Workers exposed to benzene had reduced white blood cell and platelet counts, including at levels below the United States legal limit of one part per million. In 2010, Smith and Stephen Rappaport published an article in Science on the exposome and its relation to disease risks. Their definition of exposures included chemicals produced by inflammation, oxidative stress and infections, as well as chemicals entering the body from air, water and food. In 2012, Smith led a subcommittee at International Agency for Research on Cancer (IARC) meetings in Lyon that proposed characteristics of established human carcinogens that were important for cancer development. In 2016, Smith was first author of a review in Environmental Health Perspectives that described ten key characteristics of human carcinogens. Both IARC and the National Toxicology Program Report on Carcinogens have used these key characteristics to assess the likelihood that a chemical or other agent is a carcinogen. Smith and others later helped develop similar lists for endocrine disruptors, metabolism disruptors, and substances that harm the heart, liver, reproductive system and immune system. On January 14, 2025, Smith gave a National Institute of Environmental Health Sciences Keystone Science Lecture on the key characteristics framework. Awards and honors Smith was elected a Fellow of the American Association for the Advancement of Science in 1994 for research on chemical toxicity in humans. The Children's Environmental Health Network named Smith the Science Honoree of its 2010 Child Health Advocate Awards. He became an elected Fellow of the Collegium Ramazzini in 2012 and is listed on its roster as an emeritus fellow. The Environmental Mutagenesis and Genomics Society presented him with its Alexander Hollaender Award in 2014. The American Conference of Governmental Industrial Hygienists gave him its Herbert E. Stokinger Award in 2024. References

title: Identification Act, 1986
text: The Identification Act was South African legislation that replaced the majority of the Population Registration Act, 1950. It introduced a new small identification book (Book of Life) and applied to all citizens of the Republic of South Africa, including Black South Africans replacing the existing pass laws and documents by repealing the Abolition of Passes and Co-ordination of Documents Act, No 67 of 195. This new legislation did not apply to Black citizens of the "independant" homelands. It continued a population register with the information collected used to generate an identification number for each person and recorded many other details of a persons life in the identification book. This act was repealed and replaced in 1997 with a new Identification Act. Content of the Act The following is a brief description of the sections of the Identification Act: Section 1 Defined the definition of key words in the legislation. The second part of the section defined what is termed by the statement, ordinary place of residence. Section 2 Defined that the director-general of Home Affairs compile and maintain a population register for the Republic of South Africa and do so from documents made available to him. Section 3 Defined the director-general's ability to reproduce documents needed for the population register, and any reproductions of original documents will be a true copy in a court of law. Section 4 Defined the persons whose name were to be included in a population register, and included all lawful permanent residents of the Republic, those person performing work for the government outside the country, foreign diplomats and their families, and South African citizens residing in the independent homeland state. Section 5 Defined the assignment of identity and birth entry numbers for everyone on the population register, and included in the identification number, their sex and date of birth, whether they were a citizen or foreigner, and the birth entry number based on the Population Registration Act, 1950, section 6. Section 6 Defined the personal particulars to be included on the population register and included birth entry number; the details required from the registration of a persons birth; their residence address and postal address from age 16, and polling district; dates of a foreigners naturalisation as a citizen of the Republic including the country and place of birth and their date of entry; marriage particulars; a recent photograph from aged 16; fingerprints from aged 16 but previous fingerprints collect would accepted for five years before being requested; any leaving permits or passports of the Republic; drivers licence; gun licences; occupation; state the choice of one of two official languages for communication; departure dates from the Republic, and death dates; and any other particulars required by the Home Affairs minister as listed via the Government Gazette. Section 7 Defined the issuing of a certificate of birth particulars after a births recording in the population register and would include the details of the birth entry number, date of issue, name, surname, sex and place of birth or in the case of a foreigner, their country of birth, and citizenship status. Any previous certificate issued prior to this law are deemed valid. Section 8 Defined the issuing of a new identification document after an application on a prescribed form to anyone aged 16 upwards, with two photographs. This section also described the contents of the new identity document and included the identification number, full name, sex, date of birth and place, and or country, citizenship, a photograph and anything else required by the minister of Home Affairs. All existing identification documents prior to this act were deemed still valid. Section 9 Defined the ability to issue a temporary identity certificate and its validity as a form of identification. title: Myoora
text: Myoora, also known as Bagatell, is a mansion located at 405–411 Alma Road in Caulfield North, in the City of Glen Eira, in the inner eastern suburbs of Melbourne, in Victoria, Australia. Built from 1886 on the traditional lands of the Bunurong people, the mansion was added to the Victorian Heritage Register on 21 October 1981 in recognition of its architectural significance; and was also added to non-statutory lists by the Victorian branch of the National Trust on 24 January 1974 and the now defunct Register of the National Estate on 14 May 1991. History Myoora was built between 1886 and 1887 for Thomas Christian, a mining entrepreneur who, together with William Levers and Frederick Pfeiffer, co-founded the highly profitable Day Dawn mine in Charters Towers, Queensland. The mansion was designed by Anketell Henderson, a partner of Reed, Henderson & Smart and was a major private commission for the firm, which was better known for designing commercial and public buildings. Myoora is important as one of the relatively few surviving mansions in the Caulfield area, once a noted nineteenth century mansion locality. The mansion is associated with the gold rush induced expansion of the Caulfield area and its elaborate and extravagant eclectic style is illustrative of architecture produced out of gold field fortune. Set on 4,745 square metres (51,070 sq ft), in 2003 the mansion, known as Bagatell, was sold by a Hong Kong Chinese family and purchased David Rodd, a co-owner of JB Hi-Fi, for A$5.1 million. At the time of its sale, it was reported that the property had six bedrooms, five bathrooms, two kitchens, a billiards room, an indoor spa, a four-car garage, a floodlit tennis court, a pool, a lookout tower, a sweeping circular staircase, and four reception rooms. Description Myoora is an asymmetrical two-storey cement rendered brick mansion that includes a slate roof and bay windows, bluestone cellar, with a four-storey tower and turret to the north and two-storey cast iron verandah to the south. The asymmetrical design of the facade is most unusual for the period. The semi-circular stair turret is a most important and distinctive feature and particularly unusual for domestic architecture in this period. At the base of the turret is a ventilation window for a two-roomed wine cellar. The top of the turret is decorated with a wide band of stucco with Tudor rose design, which matches that above the entrance portico at the base of the tower and the conical roof of the turret is surmounted by an elegant iron finial. The tower itself has an interesting cantilevered balcony with cast iron fence. The servants' wing, with its massive chimneys, has a crown of ornamental cast iron ridging. The east facade of the house has a small semi-circular corbelled balcony adjacent to a two-storey angular bay capped with a roof finial. The south facade, where the main rooms of the house are located, has a double-storey cast iron verandah with decorative columns. The interior of the house features a solid bank strongroom with steel door, an indication of Christian's goldfields interests. The house is architecturally significant for its combination of details from Continental and English Renaissance, Boom style, the Queen Anne Revival style, and also an early influence from the American Romanesque style, especially in the stair turret to the northern elevation. The asymmetrical composition of the residence, pivoting on the four-storey tower, is a notable feature of the mansion.

title: Omnia Sweidan
text: Omnia Sweidan (Arabic: أمنية سويدان) is an Egyptian filmmaker and former doctor. In 2026, she became known after posting on social media about obstetric abuse at the Al-Shatby Hospital in Alexandria, where she had been a medical student. The post went viral on social media, leading to other women talking about their own experiences of abuse at Egyptian hospitals, and led to Sweidan being charged and convicted of spreading false information. Biography Sweidan graduated from medical school in 2020. During her time as a student, she completed a three month placement in the obstetrics and gynaecology department at Al-Shatby Hospital, a public hospital owned and run by the Alexandria University. Sweidan later stopped working as a doctor and became a documentary filmmaker based in Beheira Governorate in northern Egypt. Allegations of obstetric abuse On 15 June 2026, Sweidan published a post on Facebook in which she described the "degrading, violent and potentially criminal" treatment of women seeking reproductive healthcare at Al-Shatby Hospital while she had been a medical student there in 2020. Sweidan gave examples including a woman in labour who was sexually assaulted while undergoing a medical examination; doctors refusing to treat a woman who had been raped; using "husband stitches" following childbirth; and refusing to admit a woman into intensive care after being unable to get consent from her husband or a male relative. Sweidan stated she had seen or heard about these incidents while working at the hospital, but had felt unable to challenge them at the time due to her being a student and not aware what she was seeing was not part of accepted medical practice. She concluded that her time at the hospital had been the "worst time of [her] life". Within hours, Sweidan's post went viral on social media, being shared tens of thousands of times. It also prompted other women to share their experiences of abusive care during treatment in Egyptian public hospitals, including from patients, doctors and human rights activists. The news outlet Mada Masr published interviews with various doctors who confirmed that abusive practice was widespread at public hospitals across the country. Arrest and conviction Following the spread of Sweidan's post, the head of legal affairs at Al-Shatby Hospital filed a criminal complaint against Sweidan, citing concerns about the hospital's reputation. Following this, the Egyptian fact-checking platform Matsadaash published a report including interviews with five doctors who worked at Al-Shatby Hospital between 2017 and 2023 who shared their experiences of verbal abuse, humiliation and neglectful care. Alexandria University, which ran the hospital, said it would investigate the allegations, while the Egyptian Medical Syndicate confirmed it had not received any complaints concerning the matter, but urged anyone with evidence to come forward. On 16 June 2026, the day after publishing the post, Sweidan was arrested at her home in Damanhur. Her family and lawyer reported they did not know her whereabouts until the following day, when she was presented before the prosecutor for East Alexandria and charged with "spreading false news" and "misusing a social media account". Sweidan was subsequently released after paying a 20, 000 EGP bail. Her Facebook account was deactivated following her release. Egyptian authorities referred the case to the Economic Misdemeanours Court in Dekhela. Following two hearings, on 4 July 2026 Sweidan was sentenced to a six-month suspended prison sentence, in addition to a 20, 000 EGP fine, after being found guilty of "publishing and intentionally spreading" false information about Al-Shatby Hospital. She was acquitted of charges of using social media to commit a crime; violating Egyptian family values; and damaging the reputation of hospital employees. title: Solenocarpus philippinensis
text: Solenocarpus philippinensis is a flowering plant in the family Anacardiaceae. It is native to maritime Southeast Asia. Description Solenocarpus philippinensis grows as a tree or shrub up to 45 m (150 ft) tall. The leaves are ovate, oblong or elliptic and measure up to 13.5 cm (5 in) long and 6 cm (2 in) wide. The inflorescences feature white flowers. The fruits ripen yellow and measure up to 1 cm (0.4 in) long. Taxonomy Solenocarpus philippinensis was initially described as Pegia philippinensis by the American botanist Adolph D. E. Elmer in Leaflets of Philippine Botany in 1919. In 1955, the Indonesian botanist André Kostermans transferred the species to the genus Solenocarpus. The type specimen was collected in Mindanao in the Philippines. The specific epithet refers to the Philippines. Distribution and habitat Solenocarpus philippinensis is native to the Philippines, Sumatra, Borneo, Sulawesi and New Guinea. Its habitat is in lowland and hill forests. Conservation Solenocarpus philippinensis has been assessed as least concern on the IUCN Red List. Its population is stable and it is widely distributed with no major threats noted. References

title: Susan Shalhoub Larkin
text: Susan Shalhoub Larkin is an American actress. She has worked in theatre, television and film. Her screen roles include Florence in the Netflix series Stranger Things, Luci in the NBC miniseries The Thing About Pam, Luanne Harley in Sleepy Hollow, and appearances in The Resident, and Monk. Early life and education Susan Shalhoub Larkin was born and raised in a Lebanese Christian household, in Green Bay, Wisconsin. Her father, Joseph, was from Zahle and immigrated to the United States as a child after his own parents, Milhem and Mariam, died during World War I, when Lebanon was still part of the Ottoman Empire. After immigrating to America, Joseph became a meat peddler who drove a refrigerated truck. Joseph married Helen Seroogy, a Lebanese American. The two met when Joseph was taken in to be raised by her family, when both were young. The Seroogy family operated a candy store that remains a family business. Career In August 1966, Larkin moved from New York to Atlanta with puppeteers Vincent Anthony and Mitchell Edmonds to establish the touring puppet company Vagabond Marionettes. The three also auditioned for the defunct Theatre Atlanta, where they were hired as actors and scenic artists. Their first production with the theatre was The Royal Hunt of the Sun. She was in Red, White and Maddox, which opened in Atlanta in 1968 and transferred to Broadway's Cort Theatre; Larkin remained in Atlanta. Larkin is active in the Atlanta theatre community in Roswell, Georgia. She appeared in the Atlanta theater Theatrical Outfit's Two Drink Minimum in 2012, and in the Georgia Ensemble Theatre's production of Emlyn Williams's Night Must Fall in 2019. Her association with the Georgia Ensemble Theatre led to a 2023 benefit performance of A. R. Gurney's Love Letters featuring her brother Tony Shalhoub and his wife Brooke Adams. In 2023, Larkin appeared in Stephen Karam's The Humans at Theatrical Outfit. She also appeared in 2022 in Actor's Express's production of Joshua Harmon's Prayer for the French Republic. Larkin's screen work include the 2002 film Made-Up. She appeared as Paulina in an episode of Monk in 2008 and as Nurse H. Josephs in the 2010 film Feed the Fish. Her film work includes roles in Good Deeds and Last Vegas. In 2013 she appeared as Luanne Harley in an episode of the television series Sleepy Hollow. From 2016 to 2019, Larkin played Florence in Stranger Things. She appeared as Shelby Waverly in the 2018 American medical drama The Resident. In 2022, Larkin played Luci in four episodes of the true-crime miniseries The Thing About Pam. In 2025, she appeared in the 2025 film Hello Beautiful. Selected filmography Personal life Susan met architect James Anthony Larkin in Atlanta in 1968. They married on 31 May 1969, and had three sons. James Larkin died on 7 May 2022. She is the sister of actors Tony Shalhoub and Michael Shalhoub. She introduced Tony Shalhoub to acting by recruiting him, when he was six, for a high-school production of The King and I in which she was appearing.

title: Douglas Arms Hotel
text: The Douglas Arms Hotel is a Grade II listed former public house on Ogwen Terrace, High Street, in Bethesda, Gwynedd, Wales. Dating from around 1820, it was originally built as a coaching inn to serve travellers using the road to Holyhead. The building retains much of its early 20th-century character and is recognised for its historic pub interior, which is included on the Campaign for Real Ale (CAMRA)'s National Inventory of Historic Pub Interiors. The pub closed in 2023 following the retirement of its owners. Its future use remains uncertain. History The building is an early 19th-century coaching inn, thought to have been constructed to serve travellers using Thomas Telford's newly established turnpike road to Holyhead. It opened around 1820. The pub was owned by the same family from 1913 until its closure in 2023. Refurbishment took place in 1930, and the interior subsequently changed relatively little, retaining four main rooms. The full-sized table in the billiard room was moved there from an upstairs room around 1934. It is also associated with snooker plus, a variation of the game introduced by Joe Davis in 1959. On 24 April 1997, the Douglas Arms Hotel was designated a Grade II listed building. The Campaign for Real Ale (CAMRA) describes its interior as being of "outstanding national historic importance" and awards it three stars on its National Inventory of Historic Pub Interiors. The pub was put on the market in April 2022. According to CAMRA, it closed following the retirement of its owners. Its future use remains uncertain. Architecture Exterior The building has white-rendered exterior walls and a slate roof, with prominent chimneys at either end. It has three floors and a symmetrical front with three main sections of windows. The roof consists of two parallel sections, with a large raised roof feature at the centre. The front elevation has rows of sash windows, with their size and design varying between floors. The main entrance is positioned centrally and consists of double wooden doors beneath a glazed panel. It is framed by a classical-style porch with columns and a decorative top. The side walls have a similar arrangement of doors and windows, although the entrance on the south-east side is raised above ground level to accommodate the slope of the site. The north-west end has an unpainted rough-textured finish. Metal railings with pointed tops stand on either side of the main entrance. Interior The pub contains four main rooms, retaining elements of its historic interior and original layout. Much of the interior dates from the early 20th century, with a number of period features still in place. The entrance opens into a hallway containing an old serving area. The interior also includes a half-glazed door with glass panels on either side and above, four-panelled doors, simple decorative mouldings and a staircase with plain wooden balusters, positioned to the right of the hall. The public bar is located towards the rear of the building. Behind the counter is a wooden bar fitting dating from the early 20th century, incorporating numerous drawers and a display of spirit jars. The room also contains curved wooden benches, a red leather bench and a fireplace dating from the 1920s. A speaking tube, formerly used to communicate with the kitchen below, remains near the bar. The billiard room is situated at the rear of the building. It contains a full-sized billiard table, transferred from an upstairs room around 1934, along with wooden bench seating and an early 20th-century tiled fireplace. A serving hatch connects the room with the bar area. Two further rooms are located at the front of the building. The room on the left is used for dining and functions and contains a fireplace with tiled and marble surrounds. The room on the right, known as the smoke room, has wooden seating and a fireplace with a 1930s Art Deco-style surround.

title: Bandhu (2026 film)
text: Bandhu (transl. Brother) is a 2026 Indian Marathi-language family drama film written and directed by Nitin Supekar. Presented by Rajat Bedi, the film is produced by Pranav Desai, Juhi Desai and Kuldeep Sunil Ojha under the banners of Kartavya Motion Pictures, JSD Studio and Triflix Entertainment. It stars Upendra Limaye and Jitendra Joshi as two brothers, alongside Mrunmayee Deshpande and Mitalee Jagtap Varadkar as their respective wives. The film follows two estranged brothers whose dispute over ancestral land creates tensions within their families. Bandhu was announced in June 2024. It was released theatrically on 20 November 2026 and received positive reviews from critics. Plot Mahadev Nangare and Sadashiv Nangare are brothers who fall out while trying to secure ownership of their inherited ancestral land. The story is told from the viewpoint of Ganesh, Sadashiv's young son, and follows the childhood of Ganesh and his brother Kartik as the quarrel pulls the two households apart. The film asks whether the rift between the brothers can be healed. Cast Upendra Limaye as Mahadev Nangare Jitendra Joshi as Sadashiv Nangare Mrunmayee Deshpande as Uma Mitalee Jagtap Varadkar as Vandana Renuka Daftardar as Muktabhai Smita Tambe as Vidya maushi Shaurya Patil as Ganesh (Ganu) Nangare Vitthal Kale as Ganesh (Ganu) Nangare (adult) Shrikant Yadav as Shrikant Tapkire Yashpal Sarnat as Santosh Dnyanratna Ahiwale as Shyam Sundar Pawar Chaitanya Solankar as Vasudev Nikam Shripad Panse as Gajanan Devle Deva Gadekar as bridegroom Varsha Ajit as bride Prashant Jadhav as bridegroom's father Anil Kamble as PI Madan Pranali Bhalerao as Madhuri Production Bandhu is the third directorial venture of Nitin Supekar, following Aatpadi Nights and Sarla Ek Koti. Principal photography began in June 2024, with filming taking place in Phaltan and Wai. Soundtrack The film's music and background score is composed by Vijay Narayan Gavande, while its music rights were acquired by Zee Music Marathi. Release The film's official poster was unveiled on 21 August 2026, featuring the two lead actors seen from behind and bearing the tagline "राम आहे म्हटल्यावर लक्ष्मण तर येणारच!" The official trailer was released on 30 October 2026 at a launch event attended by Union Minister of State Ramdas Athawale. Bandhu was released in theatres on 20 November 2026. Reception Sujit Shirke of Lokmat also gave 3.5 out of 5 stars, describing it as a "stand out film". Kalpeshraj Kubal of Maharashtra Times gave 3 out of 5 stars, writing that "Bandhu is not just a film about the conflict between two brothers, but also a film that makes children realize how children have to pay the price for the events that happen in the world of adults." Santosh Bhingarde of Sakal awarded the film 3.5 out of 5 stars, describing it as a "touching story" and praising how "Supekar has beautifully woven the threads of various relationships in this film."

title: Lego Monkie Kid (TV series)
text: Lego Monkie Kid is an animated fantasy action-adventure television series inspired by the Monkey King and Journey to the West and produced by Flying Bark Productions from seasons 1–4 and WildBrain Studios from season 5 to coincide with the release of the Lego theme of the same name. The series premiered in China on 30 May 2020 and comprises five seasons of 50 episodes in total, along with four specials. Premise Lego Monkie Kid is inspired by the Monkey King and Journey to the West, which focuses on Monkie Kid and his friends, battling against a variety of demons who are trying to take over Megapolis. Characters Main characters Monkie Kid: A young noodle delivery boy chosen by the Monkey King as his successor, inheriting his magical staff and powers. Mei: MK's best friend and a descendant of the White Dragon Horse. Pigsy: The owner of Pigsy's Noodles and a father figure to MK. Sandy: A former soldier and peaceful river ogre accompanied by his pet cat, Mo. Tang: A customer at Pigsy's Noodles who tells MK stories about the Monkey King. Monkey King: The legendary hero of the Journey to the West, who trains MK as his successor. Major antagonists Demon Bull King: The leader of the Demon Bull Family and the main antagonist of the first season. Princess Iron Fan: The wife of the Demon Bull King and mother of Red Son. Red Son: A scientist with fire powers who occasionally assists MK against greater threats. Spider Queen: The main antagonist of the second season, who seeks to conquer Megapolis. Lady Bone Demon: The main antagonist of the third season, who seeks to remake the realms in her image. Macaque: A former friend and rival of the Monkey King who eventually becomes an ally of MK. Azure Lion: The leader of the Brotherhood and main antagonist of the fourth season, who seeks to replace the Jade Emperor. The Nine-Headed Demon: The main antagonist of the fifth season, who seeks to return to the realm of chaos. Broadcast The series premiered on TV3 in Malaysia on 13 September 2020, debuted on Channel 9 in Australia on 13 March 2021, on CITV on 9 May 2022 and Boomerang on 4 February 2023 in the United Kingdom. Episodes Series overview Season 1 (2020) Monkie Kid: A Hero is Born (2020) Monkie Kid: A Hero is Born is a 45-minute television special that premiered on RTM TV2 and TV3 in Malaysia on 13 June 2020, debuted on Mediacorp in Singapore on 27 June 2020, premiered on 9Go! in Australia on 13 March 2021, and premiered internationally on Amazon Kids+ on September 9, 2021. It also debuted on CITV in the United Kingdom on 9 May 2022. Episodes Season 2 (2021) Revenge of the Spider Queen (2021) Revenge of the Spider Queen is a four-part television special that premiered on TV3 in Malaysia on 27 March 2021, premiered on 9Go! in Australia on 24 April 2021, and premiered internationally on Amazon Kids+ on October 1, 2021. It also debuted on CITV in the United Kingdom on 17 May 2022. Episodes Season 3 (2022) Embrace Your Destiny (2022) Embrace Your Destiny is a four-part television special that premiered on CITV in the United Kingdom on 1 June 2022. Season 4 (2023) The Emperor's Wrath (2023) The Emperor's Wrath is a four-part television special that premiered in China on 1 June 2023, and on the HappyKids app on 19 June 2023. Season 5 (2024) Reception Stephanie Morgan for Common Sense Media gave the animated series a three out of five star rating and commented, "This animated Lego series is fast-moving, suspenseful, and frenetic, all things that will draw young, hero-loving viewers to it. The Lego Monkie Kid episodes are short, usually around 10 minutes, but each manages a satisfying story arc and a few laughs. Unfortunately, some of those laughs come from mild violence, name-calling, or yelling. Underlying lessons are also delivered as mixed messages. For example, MK breaks something and says "part of being a hero is owning up to your mistakes," but later fails to admit what he's done. Overall, there's not a lot of bang for your parental buck here

title: Isak Gifting
text: Isak Gifting (born 25 December 2000) is a Swedish professional motocross racer. He has competed full-time in the Motocross World Championship since mid-way through the 2020 season. Following strong performances in the European Motocross Championship, Gifting was picked by the factory Gas Gas team to be a replacement rider for the injured Simon Längenfelder in the second half of the 2020 season. He stayed with the squad for a second season in 2021, before spending his final two seasons in MX2 with a British and French-based team respectively. Since moving to the MXGP class in 2024, he has raced for the JK Racing Yamaha team. Due to where his teams have been based, Gifting has competed in national championships alongside his world championship commitments. As a result, he won the 2023 British Motocross Championship in the MX2 class and the 2025 Italian Prestige Motocross Championship in the MX1 class. Gifting has represented Sweden at the Motocross des Nations on five occasions, with the most recent coming at the 2026 edition. In his debut at the 2021 edition, he was able to finish as the third best individual rider in his class. As a junior rider, Gifting was a two-time Swedish national champion in the 125cc class. Career Junior career After starting in the sport at a young age, Gifting progressed through the junior ranks in Sweden and around Europe. In 2013, Gifting finished runner-up in the 85cc class of the Swedish national championship and competed in the FIM Junior World Championship, where he scored four points in the 85 class. The following year, he returned to the Junior World Championship, this time in the 125 class. Gifting moved up to compete on a 125cc motorcycle full-time for 2015, where he concentrated on the category within the Swedish championship, scoring two third-place finishes as the highlight in the series. Gifting made his debut in the EMX125 class of the European Motocross Championship during the 2016 season, riding in four rounds only but recording four top-ten race finishes. In the first race at the second round in Italy, Gifting mixed it with the front runners to finish fourth. In Sweden, Gifting won the first two rounds of the 125cc U17 championship and despite only winning one further race throughout the series, became national champion in the class. Gifting improved his EMX125 results further during the 2017 European Motocross Championship, finishing fifth overall at the second round and scoring his first podium in the class with third overall at the fifth round in Italy. After not participating at three rounds, he finished thirteenth in the final standings. Domestically, he was able to successfully defend his 125cc U17 national title, winning all but three races throughout the season. Gifting also represented his country at the Motocross of European Nations, where the team finished seventh in the final standings. Crowned Swedish 125cc Youth National Champion in 2016 and 2017. 250 career Gifting moved up to compete on a 250cc motorcycle in 2018, riding a partial EMX250 campaign in the 2018 European Motocross Championship. Over the four rounds contested he scored forty-four points and finished ninth overall at the Latvian round. Riding in the MX2 class of the Swedish Motocross Championship, he would finish second overall at the opening round and win the first race of the season. Gifting scored a further race win at the second round and three other top-three race finishes but ended the season sixth after missing several rounds. His first full-time campaign in the EMX250 class came during the 2019 European Motocross Championship, where he finished fourteenth in the final standings. Gifting improved as the season went on, moving from not scoring points at the opening round to finishing fifth overall at the final round in his native Sweden.
